001 README.md

# PartsIQ single workflow Snowflake build kit

This kit specifies the complete69-feature PartsIQ application with a conventional Python workflow. It replaces the earlier multi-agent design while retaining the customer, staff, catalogue, analytics, security and recruiter-demo features. Voice and quotation building remain excluded.

This is an implementation kit, not a completed or deployed application. Follow 97 detailed prompts in prompts/README.md: foundations00–21 and23–25,featuresF01–F69,then final gates22 and26–27. Source contracts, SQL and dependency locks are supplied as exact implementation inputs. Test receipts must be produced by the coding agent as it builds the application.

## Start here

1. Read AGENTS.md and docs/CONTEXT.md.
2. Read docs/PRD.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/DATA_OWNERSHIP.md.
3. Create your project repository and place this kit at its root. Keep references/legacy-backend.zip unchanged.
4. Open prompts/README.md and execute prompt 00 first. Do not paste all 97 prompts into one coding-agent turn.
5. Give the agent the complete current prompt and permission to inspect the repository. After each step, require real tests, a commit, and an updated handover.
6. Enable live Snowflake/OpenAI only after confirmed account allowance checks. Explicit fixture mode runs synthetic demos without either provider.

## What is included

- 97 implementation prompts and69 feature traces.
- PRD, architecture, workflow, REST API, security, Snowflake, data ownership, deployment, rollback and handover documents.
- Typed Python models and a machine-readable OpenAPI3.1 specification.
- Supabase and Snowflake DDL, dependency manifests and resolved reference locks.
- The original backend, logo/brand pack and collaboration field guide.
- A regenerated complete guide and checksums for the archive contents.

## Locked product choices

Next.js on Vercel; Supabase Auth, PostgreSQL and Storage; one FastAPI application plus a worker from the same image; Redis for rate limits and wakeups; Snowflake for versioned catalogue source and reporting; OpenAI for extraction, vision and constrained prose; optional BGE-M3 inside the worker search module. No LangGraph or autonomous agent routing.

Snowflake's trial is time/credit limited, not a permanent free plan. AWS eligibility and Vercel plan terms are account specific. The local fixture profile is the no-provider-cost fallback and must always be labelled accurately. The kit does not activate accounts, spend credits or claim production readiness by itself.

002 AGENTS.md

# Coding agent instructions

## Mission and authority

Build PartsIQ from this single-workflow Snowflake edition. The term agent in this file means the coding assistant executing prompts; it does not authorize an AI-agent architecture in the product. Preserve all 69 features. No supervisor, specialist team, LangGraph, LangChain, CrewAI or LLM tool-calling loop is required or allowed by this design.

Authority order: current user instructions, these rules, docs/CONSTRAINTS.md, approved architecture/ADRs, typed contracts/SQL/API specification, current prompt. If two approved specifications conflict, report the concrete conflict and propose a minimal repair before implementing incompatible behavior. Do not silently reinterpret an unknown business rule.

## Work method

Execute one prompt at a time in spec/build-order.json. Read its prerequisites and current docs/HANDOVER.md. State the planned files, interfaces and tests; routine reversible implementation is authorized. Inspect existing code before writing. Preserve the supplied legacy archive and port its tested search logic into the single package instead of recreating it from memory.

Use rg to locate symbols. Prefer small cohesive functions with typed inputs and explicit side effects. Routers handle transport; feature facades handle user cases; domain modules own decisions; repositories handle persistence. Do not put SQL or credentials in React components. Do not copy compatibility, approval or budget rules into feature modules.

For every task: implement the specified behavior, run focused tests, inspect the diff, record real evidence, commit, update handover and feature traces. A file named test does not prove a behavior passed. Never fabricate test counts, accuracy, latency, production use, customer adoption or recorded videos. A blocked provider check is not passed.

## Critical invariants

1. Resolve a confirmed machine configuration before ranking its compatible part set.
2. Only activate a Snowflake catalogue version after explicit validation and atomic PostgreSQL serving-cache publication.
3. Missing information and close candidates produce questions or staff review, not guesses.
4. No recommendation is published without a current revision-bound human decision and audit record.
5. Customer identity and staff roles derive from verified authentication and server-side records.
6. Every durable job completion is fenced by lease token, revision and demo generation.
7. AI budget reservation happens before every external attempt; uncertain usage stays reserved until reconciled.
8. No paid fallback, no voice, no quotation builder, no orders/reservations, no external messages.

## Tools and dependencies

Use the package pins and locks supplied in spec. Do not install a new library merely because its API is convenient. If a pinned dependency fails on the target runtime, record the failure and propose the smallest justified change with a new lock and tests. Never loosen all pins to make a resolver pass.

Use a disposable local database for tests. Never run schema resets, seed scripts or destructive queries against production. Keep secrets in ignored environment files or provider secret stores. Do not echo keys, JWTs, signed URLs or database passwords into logs. No runtime uses the schema-owner credential.

## Completion format

Report changed behavior, paths, commands and actual results, remaining blockers, and commit. Append docs/SESSION_LOG.md. Update docs/HANDOVER.md with the next prompt. Feature traces remain specified until tests and implementation exist. Stop to clarify only when blocked by an actual missing business decision, required credential/account access or destructive operation; continue all other authorized work.

004 MASTER_PROMPT.md

# Start or resume implementation

You are implementing the PartsIQ single-workflow Snowflake edition from this repository. Read AGENTS.md, docs/CONTEXT.md, docs/HANDOVER.md and prompts/README.md. Identify the first uncompleted prompt in spec/build-order.json. Inspect its prerequisites and current source before editing.

Complete that prompt in full: typed contracts, domain behavior, REST adapters, UI where specified, permissions, failure handling, tests, documentation and commit. Preserve all 69 features and the fixed compatibility/human approval rules. No agent framework is part of the runtime. Use Snowflake only through the catalogue/reporting adapters and Supabase for operational state/auth/files. Respect the zero-paid-budget gate.

Run the prompt's named checks and record actual outcomes. Do not claim a service was deployed or a live provider was tested without execution evidence. If one external dependency blocks a check, finish independent local implementation and identify the exact missing account/configuration. Update handover and feature trace before returning. Never shorten implementation to a mock UI when the prompt calls for working backend behavior.

005 docs/CONTEXT.md

# Project context

Mohammed Zuhair Hussain is building a recruiter-facing spare-parts enquiry application inspired by industrial equipment distribution in Saudi Arabia. The demonstration uses synthetic equipment, parts, stock and customers; it does not represent a commercial relationship or real TAMGO inventory. The project should demonstrate full-stack engineering, bilingual AI extraction, deterministic data validation, warehouse planning, REST API design, data-platform integration and human review.

The original journey is retained: a Riyadh customer sends Arabic/English text and a nameplate photo; the system extracts details, confirms identifiers, identifies the machine, filters compatible parts, asks about ambiguity, plans available quantities, drafts a reply, and pauses for staff approval. Staff corrections are auditable and can support reviewed evaluation cases.

The earlier multi-agent implementation plan was explicitly replaced on16 October 2026. All 69 feature groups remain. Application orchestration now means ordinary Python functions and a persisted finite-state workflow. There are no specialist agents and no model-selected next steps. AGENTS.md describes how an external coding assistant should work on the repository, not runtime agents.

Snowflake was requested as the data-platform addition. Adopted design: immutable catalogue source versions and redacted analytical events in Snowflake; operational records, auth, files and validated relational serving cache in Supabase. This preserves PostgreSQL compatibility constraints and avoids expensive warehouse queries on every chat poll. Feature behavior must be identical between a validated live snapshot and an explicitly selected synthetic fixture snapshot, apart from provenance and freshness indicators.

Budget remains zero paid spend. The owner says they have free OpenAI keys, but provider allowance and expiry still require confirmation. Snowflake trial availability cannot be assumed permanent. Live services are disabled by default. Fixture mode must never be presented as a successful live Snowflake/OpenAI integration test.

006 docs/PRD.md

# Product requirements document

## Purpose and success criteria

PartsIQ helps customers describe equipment spare-part needs and helps staff prepare a defensible response. The system reduces manual interpretation and catalogue searching while keeping compatibility, quantity allocation and final approval under deterministic control. A successful recruiter demonstration shows the full enquiry journey, one ambiguity case, one incompatible request and one warehouse split, including visible provenance and human review.

Acceptance is behavioral rather than a claimed accuracy number: an incompatible exact-number match must never be recommended; unconfirmed photo identifiers must not drive matching; ambiguous candidates must not be silently selected; an unassigned reviewer must not see real enquiries; and a recommendation must not publish without a matching approved revision. Performance and extraction accuracy are measured later using the supplied evaluation plan.

## Actors and permissions

Public visitor reads the landing page and architecture. Anonymous demo customer owns an expiring demo session and can switch to reviewer presentation only for that session. Invited customer owns real enquiries when real onboarding is enabled. Reviewer sees assigned real enquiries and can correct, draft, approve or reject. Catalogue administrator stages, validates and publishes source versions. Administrator manages assignments, allowances, evaluation curation and aggregate reporting. Runtime worker identities are technical roles, not human roles.

## Main user journey

Customer creates an enquiry with destination warehouse and up to20 requested items. Optional images are privately uploaded, validated and read in the background. Structured extraction preserves the original message and source spans. The customer confirms photo identifiers and answers missing-information questions. Machine identification resolves one configuration. Search retrieves only explicitly compatible parts and supplies evidence. Close scores trigger a choice or review. Fulfilment combines repeated-part demand across items and reports availability, shortage and transfer estimates without reserving stock. A constrained draft is verified and presented to staff. Approval rechecks revision, catalogue and stock before atomically recording the decision and publishing the customer reply. Approved information can be exported as a bilingual enquiry PDF.

## Complete feature scope

Every feature below remains mandatory unless its behavior explicitly describes a capability flag, such as optional semantic ranking. Optional capability means implemented and testable with a transparent disabled mode, not silently omitted.

### F01 Branded landing

Explain the enquiry-to-approval journey; show synthetic-demo notice; expose Start demo and architecture links; display the supplied bilingual logo without stretching.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing repository link hides that action; logo has meaningful alternative text; no affiliation claim.

### F02 Demo scenarios and assets

Seed four deterministic scenarios: mixed-language photo, missing serial, incompatible part, local shortage; derive identifiers from seed 42; validate expected outcomes against generated records.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Reject a scenario whose expected part lacks compatibility; reject stock claims not supported by fixture quantities.

### F03 Demo role switching

Switch the presentation between customer and reviewer using the same anonymous identity and session; authorize review only for enquiries belonging to that active session.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Forged reviewer role never grants staff membership; another visitor's enquiry returns 404.

### F04 Demo isolation

Bind each session to verified anonymous Supabase identity; check generation and expiry on every read, write and worker completion; exclude demos from operational metrics by default.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Expired, reset and foreign sessions fail; missing identity context returns no rows.

### F05 Demo reset

Lock session; increment generation; cancel unfinished jobs from prior generation; enqueue Storage cleanup; keep minimal audit; create fresh scenario enquiries on explicit selection.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Late OCR from old generation cannot update current data; repeated reset idempotency key returns the same generation.

### F06 Responsive layouts

Support 360, 768, 1280 CSS-pixel widths; stack review panels; horizontally scroll comparison tables within their region; preserve sticky primary review actions without covering content.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No page-wide horizontal overflow; zoom 200 percent remains usable; mobile dialogs retain visible close action.

### F07 Arabic and English interface

Use a locale cookie and complete en/ar message catalogs; persist preference; set document lang and dir; isolate serials, numbers and part identifiers with bdi.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing translation fails tests; language switch preserves enquiry ID and unsent draft; mixed Arabic identifiers remain readable.

### F08 Light and dark themes

Use CSS semantic tokens; initialize from saved preference then system setting; expose accessible toggle; honor reduced motion and browser color-scheme.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No hydration mismatch; chart colors and focus rings meet contrast checks; storage-disabled browsers still work.

### F09 Bilingual chat

Accept Arabic, English and mixed text; preserve original message; detect preferred reply locale; render customer messages immediately after successful persistence.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Empty and oversized input returns validation error; HTML is escaped; retry does not duplicate a message.

### F10 Structured extraction

Extract item descriptions, quantities, urgency and machine hints with strict structured outputs; preserve source spans; missing quantity becomes a clarification rather than assumed order quantity.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown keys and invalid quantities reject the response; unsupported model output cannot progress to search.

### F11 Clarifying questions

Use workflow reason codes to choose code-owned bilingual questions; persist pending question; associate answer with item; rerun affected resolution only.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No final recommendation before approval; contradictory answer requires confirmation; repeat event creates one question.

### F12 Conversation memory

Persist all messages and typed current state; compact context using retained structured facts; resume by enquiry/revision; never mix customer sessions.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Restart retains unresolved questions; old revision events are ignored and audited; foreign thread ID denied.

### F13 Private uploads

Create pending attachment and unique object path; use signed upload; validate actual bytes and magic type after confirmation; strip EXIF and cap decoded pixels before OCR.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Wrong MIME, oversized content, image decompression bomb, duplicate confirmation and nonexistent object handled explicitly.

### F14 Nameplate OCR

Read validated nameplate via OpenAI vision; return model_text, serial_text, issues and source attachment; persist result only with current lease and revision.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unreadable fields remain null; vision instructions in photo are untrusted; timeout is bounded and creates recoverable status.

### F15 OCR confirmation

Show cropped or original nameplate beside extracted identifiers; require user confirm or correction; record actor and time; preserve leading zeros in serial text.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unconfirmed OCR never authorizes matching; blank corrected serial triggers missing-serial flow; stale confirmation returns 409.

### F16 Photo quality feedback

Check decodability, dimensions and blur heuristic before paid call; return actionable retake instructions; mark heuristic as advisory; allow a readable image despite noncritical blur warning.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unsupported format rejected; dark or low-resolution sample gets guidance; no fabricated OCR confidence percentage.

### F17 Multi-part enquiries

Track up to 20 items with independent quantity, machine, candidate selection and status; clarify individual items; verify aggregate allocation for repeated part requests.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: One unresolved item blocks final all-items approval; allocations across duplicate parts cannot double count available stock; zero quantity rejected.

### F18 Progress timeline

Show persisted stages, wait reason and last update; poll with bounded backoff; reconnect using server state; separate waiting for customer from waiting for staff.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No fake completed progress; failed poll retains last state and offers retry; hidden tabs reduce polling.

### F19 Enquiry history

Return cursor-paginated owned history with status and created time; filter active demo generation; link to full conversation; use stable created_at/id ordering.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Foreign owner ID ignored; invalid cursor returns 422; equal timestamps do not duplicate or skip records.

### F20 Machine identification

Preserve identify_machine logic for model, serial and rating; return resolved configuration or explicit missing/ambiguous status; normalize numeric serial only after preserving input.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Boundary serials match exactly one configuration; overlapping ranges fail Snowflake publication validation and PostgreSQL serving-cache insertion; conflicting hints never silently override.

### F21 Machine mismatch detection

Compare model and serial together; return mismatch reason with safe next question; prevent retrieval while identity unresolved.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Valid serial of a different model does not match requested model; nonnumeric serial handled without crashing.

### F22 Compatibility gate

Fetch authoritative fitment set first; rank only members; carry source_reference and catalogue version through every candidate.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: A perfect lexical match outside fitment is absent; empty fitment returns unavailable; blank provenance cannot be published.

### F23 Aliases and typo matching

Preserve Arabic normalization, part-number keys, phrase scoring and fuzzy token matching; remove machine terms using resolved model context.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Arabic part words are not removed as machine words; exact part number outranks unrelated fuzzy alias; normalization parity test matches SQL.

### F24 Semantic retrieval

Load one BGE-M3 encoder in the worker search module; use normalized 1024-d vectors; retain legacy weighted fusion; fall back to lexical on unavailable embedding path.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Wrong dimension rejected; no model loaded in API process; no semantic candidate outside compatible IDs.

### F25 Ranked candidates

Return top candidates with lexical/semantic evidence and deterministic tie order; compute runner-up margin before applying response limit.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Limit one still reports ambiguity; empty set returns no candidate; NaN scores rejected.

### F26 Ambiguity handling

Use tested score and margin thresholds in code; ask customer to distinguish fuel filter versus separator; allow staff to select only verified candidates.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: LLM cannot override low confidence; unavailable candidate choice returns 409; thresholds evaluated on labelled cases.

### F27 Match explanations

Show actual alias, machine configuration, supersession chain and fitment reference; derive explanations from search evidence rather than invented model prose.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Absent evidence shown as unavailable; user HTML is escaped; scores never labelled calibrated probability.

### F28 Compatibility references

Resolve source_reference to version-specific document and page; retain citation with every candidate and approval snapshot.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing source file blocks evidence viewer and flags review; mismatched version fails verification.

### F29 Evidence page viewer

Authorize assigned reviewer or own demo reviewer; request short-lived backend-signed PDF URL; open exact cited page; label synthetic document.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Customer receives reference only; arbitrary Storage key rejected; expired link can be renewed after authorization.

### F30 Old part numbers

Follow supersession chain with cycle protection; display old and current numbers; verify current successor has explicit fitment for resolved configuration.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Cycles rejected; inactive terminal part returns unavailable; inherited compatibility without source is rejected.

### F31 Candidate comparison

Compare two or three candidates from the same item/revision; show number, names, evidence and warehouse availability; selecting a candidate sends its ID, not browser-authored facts.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Foreign candidate or stale revision rejected; missing attribute shown as unavailable; keyboard navigation works.

### F32 Warehouse stock

Show available quantity as on_hand minus reserved; include timestamp and warehouse name; keep display and planner using same snapshot.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Negative stock blocked; stock unavailable never displayed as zero without explanation; unknown warehouse rejected.

### F33 Fulfilment planning

Allocate local stock first then reachable warehouses deterministically; compute shortage; use quantity units; do not reserve stock or create orders.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Total allocations never exceed request or stock; fractional quantities respect unit policy; unavailable transfer route cannot be invented.

### F34 Transfer estimates

Carry integer transfer_days from approved route; show estimate and source warehouse; local availability means zero transfer days.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No route gives unknown/unavailable plan rather than invented one-day promise; estimate labelled non-guaranteed.

### F35 Stock freshness

Compare stock timestamp with configurable freshness limit; mark stale data in review; re-read current stock during approval; invalidate plan when allocation no longer possible.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Future timestamp flagged; changed stock returns 409 and reruns planning; stale stock never becomes a delivery guarantee.

### F36 Staff inbox

List assigned operational enquiries and own active demo enquiries; filter status, priority, overdue and text; paginate stably; show counts in same access scope.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unassigned real enquiries hidden from reviewer; admin can see all; filters do not leak global counts.

### F37 Review workspace

Assemble current extraction, items, candidates, evidence, stock, draft and timeline; show verification failures; separate staff-only notes from customer messages.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing panels show explicit empty states; stale revision disables approval; unassigned reviewer receives 404.

### F38 Correct extracted details

Lock enquiry; compare expected revision; apply typed allowed corrections; increment revision; invalidate derived selections/draft/approval; enqueue recomputation; record before and after.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown field rejected; old revision returns 409; correction cannot directly set approved status or invent candidate facts.

### F39 Review actions

Approve only verified current draft; edit prose through controlled schema then reverify; reject with reason; record actor and idempotency key.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Double-click publishes once; concurrent edit defeats stale approval; failed verification blocks publication.

### F40 Approval invalidation

Bind approval to revision and verified fact hash; any identity, quantity, selection or catalogue-sensitive change requires new draft and approval.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Old approval cannot authorize new revision; late workflow update cannot overwrite approved current state.

### F41 Internal notes

Append reviewer notes with author and timestamp; show only in staff workspace; prohibit customer/PDF exposure; escape rendered content.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Empty or over-4000-character note rejected; customer route never includes note text; unassigned staff denied.

### F42 Assignments

Admin assigns active reviewer or unassigns; persist assignment history atomically; access changes immediately; demo reviewer access remains session-scoped.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Non-admin assignment denied; disabled/nonreviewer assignee rejected; previous reviewer loses access on next request.

### F43 Overdue indicators

Set due_at using configurable urgent/normal thresholds; display overdue only for unresolved states; sort overdue first when requested; store all times UTC.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Approved/rejected items never overdue; daylight-saving display does not change deadline; thresholds not described as contractual SLA.

### F44 Conversation summary

Produce staff-only concise summary from authorized messages and confirmed fields; store message IDs and revision; use shared budget wrapper; regenerate on relevant change.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Outdated summary labelled stale; instructions inside messages ignored; exhausted budget leaves full conversation available.

### F45 Reply drafting

Generate greeting, explanation and closing as structured slots; code inserts all numbers and allocations; choose Arabic or English from confirmed preference.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unapproved critical facts never rendered; unsupported slots rejected; provider failure permits staff-authored controlled draft.

### F46 Verification gate

Check item/configuration/candidate membership, provenance, catalogue version, selected quantities and allocation bounds; compute canonical fact hash; store named rule results.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown part, incompatible part, stale catalogue, oversold plan and hidden extra item each fail a specific rule.

### F47 Human publication gate

Only approval service inserts recommendation messages; lock enquiry and recheck role, revision and verification; unique publication index prevents duplicates.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No background job write tool can publish; database rejects recommendation lacking matching approved decision.

### F48 Input isolation

Treat customer text, OCR and imported evidence as data; separate trusted instructions; bound inputs, transitions, steps and output size; never execute model-produced templates.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Prompt injection cannot call privileged functions, change roles or reveal secrets; model result with rogue instructions remains inert.

### F49 Audit trail

Append actor, request, entity, revision and minimal before/after metadata for AI suggestions and human changes; redact secrets and full sensitive payloads.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Application UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE fail; audit write failure rolls back approval; database-owner powers documented honestly.

### F50 Durable workflows

Persist workflow_runs and workflow_step_results in PostgreSQL; run a fixed Python transition table with durable jobs; serialize each enquiry and fence completion by revision and lease token; recover after restart without LangGraph.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Duplicate jobs cannot repeat publication; stale revisions are discarded; interrupted steps resume from committed results; no LLM chooses the next step.

### F51 Background jobs

Persist job before Redis dispatch; dispatcher claims by ID; sweeper redispatches pending/expired jobs; worker handles OCR, PDF, imports and cleanup.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Redis loss does not lose DB job; unavailable Redis rate limiter fails closed; heavy work never blocks HTTP intake.

### F52 Retry and deduplication

Claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; assign lease token; heartbeat; retry transient errors with backoff up to max attempts; fence final writes by lease token.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Expired worker cannot commit; permanent validation failure not retried; provider timeout marked uncertain and budget held conservatively.

### F53 Graceful failures

Map stable error codes to bilingual recovery guidance; distinguish validation, quota, service outage and staff-required states; preserve user input.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No raw stack traces or keys; retry only safe idempotent action; search lexical fallback clearly reported.

### F54 Access and permissions

Verify Supabase issuer, audience, signature, expiry; derive identity server-side; enforce assigned-only review; keep credentials server-side; disable public real-client signup.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Forged role claim ignored; missing context denies rows; preview cannot reach prod database; demo cannot publish shared catalogue.

### F55 Saved machines

Save confirmed model and serial with user label; list own active entries; archive entry; prefill a new enquiry but re-identify against current catalogue.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Duplicate label permitted with distinct ID; foreign ID denied; stale configuration never reused as authoritative.

### F56 Repeat enquiry

Copy customer request and confirmed hints into a new enquiry; issue new ID/revision; link origin in audit; run matching, stock and review again.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Never copy approval, allocation, draft or signed file URL; source ownership required; repeated submission deduplicated.

### F57 Catalogue browser

Read published catalogue with model/category/text filters; page results; show part detail and supersession; staff can inspect fitment and sources.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No unpublished import rows exposed; missing number returns 404; literal query cannot become SQL.

### F58 Catalogue imports

Read CSV UTF-8 or XLSX without evaluating formulas; validate row schema, references, serial overlap, supersession cycles and source evidence; show dry-run report; explicit admin publish. Stage a version in Snowflake, validate all relationships explicitly and only then activate a validated PostgreSQL serving snapshot.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Invalid batch changes no published data; file with macros/formulas rejected; 50000-row and 10MiB limits enforced; public demo cannot publish.

### F59 Catalogue versioning

Store immutable versioned catalogue records in Snowflake; verify record counts and canonical SHA256; stage the PostgreSQL serving snapshot; atomically switch the active version in a PostgreSQL transaction; retain published historical records; reconcile partial remote writes.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Two publishers cannot leave two active versions; failed publish rolls back; old approval retains immutable evidence snapshot.

### F60 Missing-parts queue

Record unresolved item once; allow assigned staff to mark investigating, resolved or unavailable with note; link back to enquiry; no automatic catalogue creation.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Resolved status requires staff explanation; foreign item denied; empty search result is not fabricated stock.

### F61 Enquiry PDF

Export approved revision only; render logo, bilingual customer text, verified selections, estimates and references; embed Arabic fonts; store private object and signed download.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Exclude notes and secrets; stale or unapproved revision rejected; long Arabic names wrap without clipping; no prices or quotation title.

### F62 Labelled evaluations

Include four demos plus Arabic, typo, serial-boundary, ambiguity, stock and injection cases; record expected compatible set and clarification outcome; run deterministic suite without API calls.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No self-reported model confidence as accuracy; evaluation fixture disjoint from examples used in prompts; failures keep actual output.

### F63 Metrics dashboard

Show volume, status, review time, clarification and labelled accuracy with denominators; separate demo traffic; filter time window; scope reviewer data to assignments. Export redacted aggregate events to Snowflake through an outbox and show reporting freshness separately from live operational counts.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Zero denominator displays unavailable; no fabricated percentage; demo traffic never silently improves operational metrics.

### F64 Latency and AI cost

Measure stages with monotonic clock; log model/token usage and estimated cost; reserve confirmed free credit before each attempt; expose consumed/reserved allowance.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown price or expired credit blocks calls; concurrent reservations cannot exceed cap; API key validity never implies free credit.

### F65 Correction feedback

List authorized before/after corrections; let admin curate anonymized labelled eval cases; record reviewer and source revision; never auto-train on unreviewed edits.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Private text excluded from exported fixtures; duplicate case source detected; unreviewed correction cannot become ground truth.

### F66 Tests and CI

Run service-isolated Python tests, frontend checks, RLS integration and deterministic evals; build images; require explicit environment approval for deployment; pin action SHAs.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No prod DB in tests; no secret available to untrusted fork jobs; failed gate blocks deployment.

### F67 Traces

Propagate request/enquiry/job IDs; capture stage timing and safe status; export optional Langfuse traces with payload redaction; operate normally when tracing unavailable.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No raw key or full photo logged; exporter outage never breaks approval; budget accounting remains local and authoritative.

### F68 Recruiter documentation

Write concise overview, real architecture, quick start, demo paths, tests, trade-offs and limitations; link measured evidence; explain deterministic decisions and ordinary Python functions.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No invented accuracy, uptime, client relationship or production adoption; distinguish implementation status from specification.

### F69 Demo walkthrough

Create 3-minute and 8-minute scripts covering happy path, missing serial, incompatibility, stock split and human review; include recording checklist and captions.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Do not claim video exists until recorded; use synthetic data; show failure handling and reset; verify links before sending recruiters.

## Nonfunctional requirements

Security: server-verified identity, scope checks, RLS, private files, least-privilege data roles, redacted logging and no model-authorized writes. Durability: database-backed jobs, leases, fencing, idempotent API writes and recoverable partial Snowflake synchronization. Language: Arabic/English UI and replies, mixed-script identifiers, bidi isolation and bundled Arabic PDF fonts. Accessibility: keyboard operation, visible focus, reduced motion, 200 percent zoom and360px minimum layout. Maintainability: typed models, one domain implementation per rule, versioned migrations and explicit test evidence.

Provisional performance goals are local acceptance budgets, not measured claims: API writes should acknowledge without waiting for AI or warehouse work; provider operations have bounded timeouts; polling uses backoff; optional embeddings cannot prevent lexical readiness. Benchmark the actual host before setting public latency claims. The paid budget is zero; the system requires confirmed free allowance before live provider calls. Real-client retention is an onboarding decision; until it is recorded, real onboarding stays disabled. Demo access expires after24hours and background cleanup follows the documented policy.

## Exclusions

No voice input, quotation builder, prices, payments, orders, stock reservations, automatic WhatsApp/email sending, multi-agent routing, autonomous SQL generation or automatic training on staff corrections. No claim of perpetual free cloud hosting. No invented partnership with equipment distributors.

007 docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

# Application architecture

## 1 What is in the system

The browser runs a Next.js application hosted on Vercel. It authenticates through Supabase and sends business REST requests to a single FastAPI backend behind Caddy. Supabase PostgreSQL stores transactional application state and a validated relational catalogue cache; Supabase Storage holds private attachments, evidence, imports and exports. A worker imports the same Python package as the API and executes durable jobs. Redis provides request-rate counters and optional wakeups. Snowflake stores immutable catalogue source versions, inventory snapshots and redacted analytical events. OpenAI performs bounded language/vision calls. BGE-M3 is an optional worker-local search capability.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
 W["Next.js customer and staff UI"] --> A["FastAPI REST application"]
 W --> S["Supabase Auth and Storage"]
 A --> P["Supabase PostgreSQL"]
 A --> R["Redis limits and wakeups"]
 P --> J["Worker using same application package"]
 J --> P
 J --> F["Snowflake catalogue and reporting"]
 J --> O["OpenAI extraction and drafting"]
 J --> S
```

## 2 Who owns each responsibility

| Module | Exact application directory | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | apps/api/partsiq/api | Typed REST endpoints, error serialization and dependency injection |
| Authentication | apps/api/partsiq/auth | JWT verification, scope, roles and demo sessions |
| Enquiries | apps/api/partsiq/enquiries | Intake, history, corrections, fulfilment, review and publication |
| Search | apps/api/partsiq/search | Legacy identification, compatibility, lexical ranking and optional embeddings |
| Workflow | apps/api/partsiq/workflow | Fixed transitions and persisted step results |
| AI | apps/api/partsiq/ai | Allowance-controlled structured extraction, vision and reply slots |
| Jobs | apps/api/partsiq/jobs | Claims, leases, dispatch, retry and cleanup |
| Catalogue | apps/api/partsiq/catalogue | Snowflake source, validation and atomic serving activation |
| Analytics | apps/api/partsiq/analytics | Redacted outbox, Snowflake export and scoped metrics |
| Storage and exports | apps/api/partsiq/storage and exports | Private signed transfers and approved PDFs |
| Features | apps/api/partsiq/features | User-case facades; no duplicated domain safety rules |
| Web | apps/web/src | Accessible bilingual pages, panels and typed API client |

## 3 Why this structure

The customer journey has a known sequence. Ordinary functions and a fixed state table are sufficient; an LLM does not need to decide which component runs next. One backend avoids multiple internal HTTP hops and duplicated deployment configuration. Background work remains separate because photo reading, imports and PDF rendering can outlive an HTTP request. Snowflake gives the project a real data ingestion/reporting boundary, while the relational serving cache preserves transactional integrity and low-cost interactive access.

## 4 What each layer may access

Routes call feature facades and inject a verified ActorContext. Facades invoke domain functions and repositories. Domain search never calls an LLM to decide compatibility. AI modules receive minimal data and return typed results; they have no database write tools. Only the approval service can create recommendation messages. Catalogue synchronization uses a dedicated publisher role; ordinary API routes cannot update published fitment rows. Snowflake connectors execute allowlisted SQL with bound values and task-scoped connections. Frontend has no Snowflake or database-owner credential.

## 5 Who owns the data

PostgreSQL is authoritative for identity linkage, enquiries, revisions, candidates, drafts, decisions, jobs, budgets, audit and the active catalogue pointer. Snowflake holds the immutable source records for catalogue versions and analytical copies. Activation copies a verified source snapshot into PostgreSQL under a single transaction; that serving copy is authoritative for a particular active version until another validated version is activated. This is an explicit replicated-data contract, not two writable masters. Stock is separately timestamped and never treated as a reservation.

## 6 Where asynchronous boundaries exist

An API mutation commits the business record and durable job together. The worker claims the job and performs external work outside database locks. It commits only if lease token, revision and demo generation still match. Redis loss does not delete jobs. Snowflake publication is a recoverable two-system process: remote immutable upload first, local validation and activation second. Analytics uses an outbox with idempotent EVENT_ID MERGE and acknowledgement after remote success. No distributed transaction is claimed.

## 7 How security and failures are contained

Every scoped route checks identity and ownership/assignment. PostgreSQL RLS provides another boundary. Background handlers load trusted job context and fence final writes. Private files require signed access after authorization. Provider errors never bypass compatibility or approval. Wrong/expired allowance blocks live AI; Snowflake outage leaves an explicitly identified last validated snapshot usable only within freshness policy. A new unpublished version cannot replace a working snapshot. If required data is too stale, the workflow pauses.

## 8 How this is tested and operated

Unit tests cover pure rules; integration tests cover real PostgreSQL constraints, RLS, idempotency and concurrency; feature tests cover all 69 behaviors; browser tests cover both languages and four demos. Live Snowflake and provider checks require separate account receipts. API and worker share one immutable image, with Caddy and Redis on one EC2 host where confirmed credits permit. Supabase dev/prod are separate projects. The host is a single point of failure; backups and recovery are documented without a high-availability claim. Fixture mode remains a clearly labelled local demonstration path.

008 docs/DATA_OWNERSHIP.md

# Data ownership and synchronization

## Source and serving responsibilities

| Data | Authoritative write owner | Read path | Consistency rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auth sessions | Supabase Auth | Verified JWT and auth service | Never trust browser role metadata |
| Enquiries and decisions | PostgreSQL application transactions | Scoped REST resources | Current revision and actor required |
| Catalogue version source | Snowflake loader | Version-addressed connector read | Immutable once accepted; hash and counts verified |
| Active catalogue | PostgreSQL activation transaction | Version-filtered relational mirror | Exactly one active pointer; no mixed versions |
| Stock snapshots | Source snapshot import | Validated serving stock rows | Timestamp and snapshot provenance retained |
| Private images/evidence/PDF | Supabase Storage | Authorized signed URLs | Bucket/object ID ownership required |
| AI allowance | PostgreSQL locked budget account | Backend budget wrapper | Reserve before call; no remote reporting dependency |
| Analytics | PostgreSQL outbox then Snowflake copy | Scoped live counts or admin warehouse reports | At-least-once transport, idempotent event key |
| Audit | PostgreSQL append-only application role | Authorized staff view | Business change and audit commit together |

## Catalogue publication protocol

1. Admin creates an import batch and uploads the file privately. Validation parses typed entities without evaluating formulas or macros.
2. Canonicalize each record by entity type, key and stable JSON encoding. Preserve numeric legacy IDs; new records receive IDs through a controlled allocator before the source snapshot is sealed. Compute each row hash and the whole snapshot hash over sorted records.
3. Validate duplicate keys, foreign references, serial-range overlap, nonblank provenance, supersession cycles, valid units and evidence file availability. Imported stock validates nonnegative quantities and timestamps independently.
4. A single publisher job obtains a bounded publication lease. Write the full immutable VERSION_ID to Snowflake. Before retry, read the existing version and require exact hash/count equality; conflicting content under the same ID is an error.
5. Read the version back through SnowflakeCatalogueRepository, validate duplicates before mapping rows, and compare observed counts/hash with the manifest. Standard table PK/FK declarations do not enforce this.
6. Stage a catalogue_syncs receipt. Begin a PostgreSQL transaction, acquire the catalogue advisory lock, and compare the caller's expected active version. Upsert relational rows in dependency order. Keep historical referenced IDs; hide removed rows using the active catalogue_records keyset. Recheck the enforced PostgreSQL constraints.
7. Retire the previous pointer and activate the new version in that same transaction. Commit the sync receipt and audit. If the transaction fails, the old version remains active and the remote version remains unactivated.
8. Pending enquiries detect a changed active version on their next processing/review action and require recomputation. Previously approved replies retain their immutable fact/evidence snapshot and are never rewritten as history.

Snowflake is not queried on every chat message or dashboard poll. The UI displays catalogue source, active version, last activation and stock observed time. Fixture mode uses the same validation contract and a different explicit source label. Never silently fall back from live Snowflake to fixtures after a failure.

## Snapshot payload contracts

The CATALOGUE.RECORDS payload uses the exact typed columns of the corresponding legacy PostgreSQL entity, excluding generated search_document and database timestamps where not business data. Supported entities: equipment_families, equipment_models, model_configurations, parts, part_aliases, part_compatibility, part_supersessions, warehouses, warehouse_transfer_routes. Key construction is deterministic: single numeric IDs use their decimal string; composite keys use compact JSON arrays of their primary-key values. A schema version is recorded in the import report. Unknown entity types/fields fail validation rather than being silently dropped.

Stock uses the dedicated Snowflake STOCK_SNAPSHOTS table. Preserve snapshot_id, observed_at and original units during serving import. One snapshot is activated transactionally only after all its rows validate. Approval checks age and availability but does not reserve stock; the final text clearly labels availability as a snapshot and delivery time as an estimate.

## Analytics transport

Business code appends an outbox event after redaction in the same PostgreSQL transaction. A single export job takes at most100 events, constructs bound MERGE statements keyed by event_id, and acknowledges only after Snowflake success. Duplicate remote IDs cause a diagnostic failure and repair; Snowflake primary-key metadata is not a uniqueness guarantee. A crash after remote commit replays the same event safely. Only allowlisted analytical columns are exported; no customer text, serial number, email, JWT, notes or signed URL enters Snowflake reporting.

Scoped live queue counts remain PostgreSQL queries. Snowflake reports are administrator-only aggregates and display sync lag. Reviewer dashboards never receive global unassigned counts. An expired trial freezes remote reporting and shows its last timestamp; it does not fabricate current metrics.

## Stock activation receipt

stock_snapshot_receipts records the source snapshot ID, observed timestamp, content hash, row count and active flag. Under the publication lock, upsert stock_levels and switch the single active stock receipt in one PostgreSQL transaction. All plan reads return that snapshot ID. Approval compares the current active stock snapshot and freshness against the draft; changed availability triggers a new plan. Do not use a null snapshot ID to hide missing provenance in live mode.

009 docs/WORKFLOW.md

# Fixed Python workflow

The controller is a deterministic transition table, not an LLM router. Persist state in workflow_runs and completed outputs in workflow_step_results. The unique key is enquiry_id plus revision. A job lease and a separate input hash fence every committed result.

| Current step | Condition | Next step | Function owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| intake | Text parsed and no image pending | identify or clarify | ai.extraction.extract_message |
| intake | Validated image requires reading | await_ocr | jobs.nameplate.read_nameplate |
| await_ocr | OCR result persisted | confirm | enquiries.extraction.confirm_nameplate |
| confirm | Customer confirms identifiers | identify | workflow.resolution.resolve_items |
| identify | Missing or conflicting machine details | clarify | enquiries.questions.clarification |
| identify | One configuration resolved for each item | search | search.service.SearchService |
| clarify | New answer accepted in new revision | intake or identify | enquiries.intake.append_message |
| search | No compatible result | needs_staff | workflow.resolution.resolve_items |
| search | Close candidates | choose | enquiries.questions.clarification |
| search | Unique sufficient match | plan | enquiries.fulfilment.plan_enquiry |
| choose | Current candidate chosen | plan | enquiries.revisions.choose_candidate |
| plan | Complete or explicitly short plan | draft | ai.reply.draft_slots |
| plan | Missing/stale inventory | needs_staff | enquiries.fulfilment.plan_enquiry |
| draft | Structured slots rendered | verify | enquiries.verification.verify_facts |
| verify | All checks pass | review | workflow.repository.commit_step |
| verify | Any rule fails | needs_staff | enquiries.verification.verify_facts |
| review | Current revision approved | complete | enquiries.approval.approve |
| review | Corrected/rejected | new revision or terminal rejection | enquiries.revisions or approval |

Each transition has a typed StepOutcome with reason_code and model-validated step data. The data envelope is not permission to store arbitrary provider output. Define a concrete payload model for each step using the provided IntakeResult, MachineView, CandidateList, PlanView, ReplySlots and VerificationResult contracts. Validate the matching payload before persistence.

## Persistence algorithm

Claim a due job with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a random lease token. Load enquiry/session and reject obsolete revision/generation. Under a short transaction, claim the matching workflow run. Release locks before calling OpenAI, Storage or Snowflake. Hash the exact step inputs and reuse only an identical completed result. Perform one bounded step. Reacquire row lock, recheck lease/revision/generation, write output and next state, append audit, then commit. Schedule the next step or park at a waiting state. Renew leases while healthy; never let an expired process finalize a result. Stop after20automatic transitions in one job.

No transaction remains open across a provider call. There is no promise of exactly-once external API execution; uncertain provider completions remain conservatively charged/reserved. Business publication is effectively once through idempotency and a unique recommendation-per-revision index.

## User changes

New facts or item choice invalidate derived data by creating a new revision. Preserve old outputs for audit but do not reuse them without matching input hash and source version. Assignment and notes need not change the extraction revision unless they alter facts. An assignment has its own audit event and immediate access effect. Reset increments demo generation and makes old jobs obsolete. User questions are code-owned bilingual templates and do not require staff approval because they make no final part recommendation.

## Cross-feature dependencies

Search and verification share one source of fitment truth. Draft rendering consumes VerifiedFacts only. Approval rechecks freshness and fact hash. PDF uses ApprovedSnapshot only. Analytics observes committed business events and cannot block approval. AI allowance remains local and authoritative even when traces or Snowflake reporting are unavailable.

## Missing quantity before item materialization

IntakeResult permits a null quantity because absence is not permission to assume one. Keep provisional item identifiers and their extracted fields in the typed workflow state until quantity is confirmed. Do not insert a null or invented quantity into enquiry_items, whose quantity constraint is intentionally positive and non-null. Clarification tracks the provisional item identifier in state; once confirmed, materialize that item with the same UUID and current revision. Persist the original extraction separately for audit. Tests must cover multiple items where only one quantity is missing.

010 docs/REST_API.md

# REST API contract

## Transport rules

FastAPI is the only business API. Base prefix is /v1. HTTPS is required outside localhost. JSON requests use Content-Type application/json. Authorization uses a Supabase Bearer token; never use a customer-supplied actor field. Every response carries X-Request-ID. Every mutating request, including DELETE, requires an Idempotency-Key UUID. The key is scoped by actor, method and path; reusing it with different payload returns 409. JSON updates carry expected_revision where specified. A POST returning202 has committed a job/resource but has not completed the background action.

Typed models in spec/contracts.py and spec/api_models.py are canonical. spec/openapi.json expands their fields and nested schemas; spec/endpoints.json declares ownership. No unknown keys are accepted. UUIDs are strings on the wire, Decimal quantities/costs are decimal strings, datetimes are ISO8601UTC and serial/part numbers remain strings. For strict Pydantic models use JSON-aware validation at the HTTP boundary; do not reject valid JSON UUID strings because a Python-only strict validator expects a UUID instance.

GET requests with Query models use validated query parameters, not a JSON body. Repeated comparison part_ids are repeated query parameters. Cursor pagination orders by(created_at, id), uses a base64url encoded typed tuple, and rejects invalid cursors. Cursor validity is not authorization; always apply scope filters. limit defaults25 and caps100. Unknown status/filter values are422. A route response is bounded; large histories are paginated and private details are separate resources.

## Access labels

public means no account. customer means any verified eligible user including an anonymous demo user with an active session where needed. demo means the subject's own active demo session. owner means the enquiry owner or authorized staff via the same scope rule. review means own-session demo reviewer, assigned real reviewer, or admin. reviewer means reviewer/admin listing only its permitted records, plus own-demo context. catalogue_admin means catalogue_admin/admin and never an anonymous demo. admin means server-side admin membership. scoped means derive ownership through the referenced job/export/resource; never authorize merely because the caller knows a UUID.

## Errors

All failures use application/problem+json with Problem fields: type, title, status, code, detail, request_id, retryable.401 means missing/invalid token; 403 means a known disallowed role action; 404 conceals a foreign scoped resource; 409 means stale revision, idempotency conflict, changed catalogue or invalid current state; 413 means size limit; 422 means input/schema validation; 429 means rate limit; 503 means required dependency or live allowance unavailable. Include Retry-After only when retry is appropriate. Never include SQL, provider payloads, secrets or internal file paths. Domain code returns named errors; only route adapters choose HTTP transport.

| F59 | GET | /v1/admin/catalogue/versions | None | VersionList | catalogue_admin | 200 |
| F60 | GET | /v1/staff/missing-parts | InboxQuery | MissingPage | reviewer | 200 |
| F61 | GET | /v1/exports/{export_id}/download | None | DownloadTicket | owner | 200 |
| F62 | GET | /v1/admin/evaluations/{run_id} | None | EvaluationView | admin | 200 |
| F63 | GET | /v1/admin/analytics/sync | None | AnalyticsSyncView | admin | 200 |
| F64 | PUT | /v1/admin/ai-allowance | AllowanceSet | AllowanceView | admin | 200 |

## Worked request and lifecycle

POST /v1/enquiries uses EnquiryCreate: text, locale, destination_warehouse_id, and optional session_id. It returns EnquiryView with id, revision, status, messages, item_ids, catalogue_version_id and updated_at. The server creates the first message and a durable workflow job in the same transaction. A client then polls GET /v1/enquiries/{enquiry_id}/progress and GET /v1/enquiries/{enquiry_id}. It does not poll Snowflake directly.

If a nameplate is present, the upload endpoint issues a ticket; the browser uploads bytes and confirms that attachment. The worker validates/reads the image and the client confirms the resulting identifiers. Once a verified draft exists, an assigned reviewer reads the staff workspace and posts ApprovalRequest. The API locks/revalidates and commits approval plus recommendation together. If the request has an old revision, it returns 409 and the UI reloads; it never silently approves a new revision.

## Route implementation pattern

Define a separate APIRouter in each owned feature route module. Use Depends for verified actor and typed command dependencies. The handler calls its feature facade exactly once, with path IDs and idempotency context. A facade calls foundation domain functions and returns the declared model. Register the router in api/router.py only after its module exists. No model-generated route, SQL or endpoint name is accepted. Keep responses free from internal notes unless this is an explicitly authorized staff-only model.

## Versioning and contract tests

The backend generates OpenAPI during CI. Compare the completed operation subset during incremental work; the final gate requires all 77 specified operations and their response schemas. TypeScript types/Zod schemas must represent the same fields. Additive fields still require a documented contract update because strict models reject unknown keys. Breaking changes require a new API version or coordinated migration; do not silently change an existing field's type.

012 docs/CONTRACTS.md

# Typed contracts

The complete executable model definitions are in spec/contracts.py and spec/api_models.py. Their JSON schemas are in spec/contracts.schema.json and the complete HTTP schema is spec/openapi.json. Copy them into partsiq.core in foundation 01. Keep nested fields, limits, enums and nullability unchanged unless a documented correction is required.

The API inventory and access rules are in REST_API.md. Foundation prompts define domain function signatures; feature prompts define facade signatures and exact wire request/response models. Decimal values are serialized as strings. Source record payloads have schema validation keyed by entity type and may never be accepted as arbitrary JSON for publication.

013 docs/SNOWFLAKE.md

# Snowflake implementation guide

## What the integration demonstrates

PartsIQ uses Snowflake for immutable catalogue ingestion, inventory snapshots and analytical reporting. This is a data-platform integration, not a replacement for Supabase authentication or a place to run an autonomous SQL agent. Interactive REST reads use the validated serving copy. The demo should visibly show source version, hash, activation time and reporting sync time so the integration is concrete.

## Exact client and API choices

Pin snowflake-connector-python4.8.0, released30 September 2026. Its installation receipt is in spec/dependency-receipts.json. Version5.0.0 was released15 October and does not meet this kit's14-day stability window. Current online docs may show5.x renamed connection parameters; the implementation must follow the pinned4.8 signature and smoke-test it. Use connect with account, user, private_key_file, private_key_file_pwd, role, warehouse, database, schema, paramstyle='qmark', login_timeout=10 and network_timeout=30. Set STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS=20 and a request-UUID QUERY_TAG through session_parameters.

Use Connection.cursor, Cursor.execute with bound values, Cursor.fetchall or fetchmany for bounded reads, Cursor.sfqid for a query receipt, and close both resources in finally. Use explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK for a logical remote write; DDL is setup-only and must not be mixed into transactional import publication. Do not share one live connection among unrelated async tasks. The connector is blocking: call it in asyncio.to_thread in the worker with at most2concurrent tasks. Cancellation of the awaiting coroutine is not proof that a remote statement stopped; retain query ID and classify uncertain completion for reconciliation.

Example read query is fixed SQL: SELECT ENTITY_TYPE, ENTITY_KEY, PAYLOAD, ROW_SHA256 FROM PARTSIQ_DEV.CATALOGUE.RECORDS WHERE VERSION_ID=? ORDER BY ENTITY_TYPE, ENTITY_KEY. Bind(str(version_id), ). Database/schema identifiers cannot be value placeholders; choose them from the fixed validated environment allowlist. JSON payloads are parsed and checked against entity schemas. No user field becomes an identifier or SQL fragment.

## Schema and roles

Apply infra/snowflake/001_schema.sql, 002_roles.sql and003_validation_queries.sql after copying them from spec. Development uses PARTSIQ_DEV and production uses PARTSIQ_PROD through the setup tool's allowlisted substitution. CATALOGUE.VERSIONS stores the version manifest; RECORDS stores typed entity records; STOCK_SNAPSHOTS stores inventory observations. REPORTING.EVENTS stores redacted events and DAILY_METRICS aggregates them. Snowflake standard tables have no application-defined indexes; do not promise PostgreSQL indexes/RLS on these tables. The initial small catalogue does not require clustering or search optimization services.

PARTSIQ_READER can read catalogue tables. PARTSIQ_LOADER has reader access plus controlled writes. PARTSIQ_REPORTER can write/read reporting events and read the report view. Each service identity has only its required role and warehouse usage. No application uses ACCOUNTADMIN, SECURITYADMIN or table-owner credentials. Loader permissions technically allow mutation, but application code rejects changing a sealed version; administrative bypass capability must be documented rather than called tamper-proof.

## Validation and publication

Run duplicate-key diagnostics before mapping rows into dictionaries. Validate referential integrity, serial ranges, supersession graph, evidence and stock in Python and again through PostgreSQL constraints on activation. Never use RELY to optimize declared constraints unless the validation pipeline actually guarantees them. The full activation protocol is in DATA_OWNERSHIP.md. An unactivated remote version has no effect on customer search. Failed activation returns an actionable import report with row/field/code and preserves the previous active data.

## Reporting and replay

Select at most100 pending analytics events from PostgreSQL. Redact to the defined reporting columns, then MERGE by EVENT_ID under a single exporter lease. Same EVENT_ID with conflicting payload is an integrity error, not a silent update. On retry, identical existing data is success. Acknowledge PostgreSQL only after Snowflake succeeds. Track query ID, row count, last success time and pending backlog. Do not export raw text or identity data. Dashboard labels distinguish live operational counts from delayed Snowflake aggregates.

## Cost and availability

The standard trial lasts30days or until free usage balance is exhausted, whichever happens first. This is not a permanent free tier. Confirm actual balance/expiry before creating or resuming a warehouse. Use one X-Small warehouse with AUTO_SUSPEND=60, AUTO_RESUME=true, INITIALLY_SUSPENDED=true and bounded statement timeouts only when allowance permits. Frequent wakeups still incur minimum resume billing; batch imports/reports and do not run warehouse queries during UI polling. Disable Cortex, Snowpipe, automatic clustering and other unneeded billable features.

A resource monitor is a guardrail, not a hard no-charge guarantee: warehouse suspension may lag and some serverless/cloud-service usage is outside its coverage. The application additionally checks the configured expiry and refuses scheduled remote work after it. Do not automatically attach a payment method or upgrade a trial. After expiry, the operator can select fixture mode explicitly or demonstrate a previously validated labelled snapshot under freshness policy; live Snowflake verification remains unavailable.

## Verification checklist

Verify key-pair login with the correct account/role, one bounded SELECT, round-trip of the synthetic catalogue, duplicate-key rejection, serial-overlap rejection, checksum mismatch, remote success/local failure, retry without duplicate reporting, expired allowance, and UI freshness labels. Save query IDs and counts without secrets. Offline fixtures verify domain behavior but are not a substitute for these live checks.
