022 docs/UI_SPEC.md

# Interface and interaction specification

Use the supplied PartsIQ bilingual logo and brand tokens. Preserve artwork aspect ratio and use the provided favicon, app and social assets. Navigation includes Home, Demo, My enquiries, Saved machines and authorized Review, Catalogue and Analytics pages. Show a persistent synthetic-demo banner and explicit data/AI mode labels.

The customer page places conversation first, with attachment preview and confirmed machine details. Render persisted progress and the pending question. Multiple items have separate quantities and statuses. Customer references expose citation text, not private evidence URLs. Distinguish approved replies from status messages. Failed submissions retain input and reuse the same idempotency key on retry.

The staff workspace includes queue, extraction, candidates, comparison, evidence, stock plan, verification, draft and approval controls. Internal notes remain staff-only. Show revision and freshness before approval. A 409 response reloads current state and requires a new intentional approval. Assignment is admin-only. Imports show row-level errors, hash, version and an explicit publication action after validation.

Provide complete English and Arabic catalogs. Set html lang/dir and isolate identifiers with bdi. Language/theme changes preserve unsent input. Support keyboard focus, descriptive labels, loading/empty/error states and accessible dialogs. At 360px, stack panels and contain wide tables in scroll regions. At 200 percent zoom, keep primary actions reachable. Honor reduced motion and system color scheme. Never display fake completion percentages or fabricated live inventory.

023 docs/DEPLOYMENT.md

# Deployment runbook

## Deployment profiles

Local fixture profile is the default and requires no live OpenAI/Snowflake account. It still runs the real application, local Supabase, private storage, workflow, search and approval; AI fixture outputs are visibly labelled. Live development profile uses Supabase dev plus confirmed OpenAI/Snowflake allowance. Hosted profile uses Next.js/Vercel and one AWS EC2 host for Caddy, API, worker and Redis. Supabase production is a separate project. Render is an alternative only if the owner explicitly selects and verifies an appropriate current plan.

## 1 Prepare local tooling

Install the target Python 3.12, Node 22.22.0, pnpm10.30.3, Docker Engine/Compose and the pinned Supabase CLI from infrastructure receipts. Create the repository, copy the kit and execute foundation 00. Preserve the original legacy archive. Copy environment.example to an ignored .env and fill only local Supabase configuration. Run supabase start and inspect the actual local endpoints. Never use a production project URL for local tests.

Run uv venv --python 3.12 and uv pip sync spec/python-requirements.lock after the files exist. Install the frontend from the frozen manifest/lock in foundation 18. Implementation prompts create the following runnable commands; they are not shipped as already completed application code in this kit.

## 2 Initialize local data

Run python tools/apply_postgres.py --environment local after its foundation implementation. It must reject a nonlocal database before applying SQL 001–006. Run python tools/seed_demo.py --source fixture --seed 42. Verify counts, hash, all four scenario expectations, and synthetic evidence assets. Keep real onboarding disabled. Start docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f infra/compose.fixture.yml up --build and run the feature tests. The API and worker must report fixture provenance; no live model call is made.

## 3 Configure Supabase dev

Create or select the development project within the owner's allowed plan. Apply migrations through the operator credential, then create least-privilege LOGIN roles mapped to API, workflow, worker, search andcatalogue groups. Store their passwords in secrets, not SQL source. Configure auth issuer/audience and JWKS verification; enable anonymous demo signin and invite named staff. Configure redirect URLs for localhost and the intended Vercel development domain. Set private bucket limits/policies from SQL 005. Verify two-user RLS and private downloads before exposing a demo.

## 4 Configure Snowflake dev

Confirm actual trial/account allowance and expiry. If unavailable, continue fixture mode and mark live integration blocked. With an authorized dev account, run the setup tool against PARTSIQ_DEV and the supplied schema/role SQL. Generate/register key-pair service-user credentials locally and store only the public key in Snowflake. Private keys remain secret-mounted files with restrictive permissions. Grant each role only the required database/schema/table and warehouse permissions.

Create one initially suspended X-Small warehouse only after allowance confirmation. Set AUTO_SUSPEND60, AUTO_RESUMEtrue and statement timeout20seconds. Attach a resource monitor based on the confirmed credit budget. Do not select an invented budget value or claim the monitor guarantees zero charges. Avoid Cortex/serverless features. Run python tools/snowflake_preflight.py --environment dev and save sanitized role/version/query receipts. Publish the synthetic source version through the same import/sync flow used by the app and compare the serving hash.

## 5 Enable approved OpenAI usage

Confirm that the owner-provided key has a dedicated free allowance and expiry for the selected text and vision models. Configure the exact accessible model IDs and pricing inputs in the admin allowance record. The key alone is insufficient evidence. Set AI_MODE=live only after preflight succeeds. Test a bounded structured extraction and one synthetic nameplate through the budget wrapper, recording token usage and reservation settlement. Leave fixture mode available as an explicit selection, never an automatic paid fallback.

## 6 Build and deploy backend

Confirm AWS account eligibility, balance, expiry and intended instance/storage/network costs. Benchmark memory before enabling BGE-M3; small free instances may not fit it. Keep semantic capability disabled transparently when capacity is insufficient, while retaining its implementation/tests. Provision only authorized covered resources. Restrict inbound ports toHTTPS/HTTP and owner-controlled SSH access; Redis and API internal ports remain private. Use the owner-controlled domain in Caddy and verifyDNS/HTTPS.

Build the immutable image with the release commit tag. Run docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f infra/compose.production.yml config to inspect interpolation without printing secret values. Pull/build approved images, run migrations as a one-off operator job, then start API, worker, Redis and Caddy. Check liveness, readiness, durable queue recovery and restricted ports. No LangGraph/search/orchestrator services are deployed. Keep a previous compatible image tag for rollback.

## 7 Deploy frontend

Connect the repository to Vercel with apps/web as the project root. Use the exact build command and packageManager from the manifest. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN and matching Supabase public values. Preview environments point todev only; production points toprod only. Private Snowflake/OpenAI/database keys never enter frontend variables. Verify CORS contains the exact deployed origin and no wildcard credential policy. Confirm the owner's current Vercel plan permits the intended demo usage.

## 8 Hosted acceptance

Execute the four demo scenarios inEnglish/Arabic from a clean browser session. Confirm photo extraction, missing serial, incorrect part refusal, warehouse split, review andapprovedPDF. Create a second anonymous visitor and prove it cannot read the first session. Reset a session during a running OCR job and prove the late result cannot reappear. Reassign a real enquiry in dev and prove old reviewer access islost. Compare source/serving version and reporting lag. Record actual timings, not invented targets. Only then mark hosted acceptance passed.

## 9 Operate within allowance

Monitor allowance expiry, worker backlog, failed jobs, stock freshness, active catalogue hash andreporting delay. Stop live scheduled work before confirmed free access expires. AWS and Snowflake free access may be temporary; local fixture mode is the durable demonstration alternative. Back up PostgreSQL andprivate evidence according to the owner-approved retention policy. Do not claim high availability for a single EC2 host. Deployment doesnot change the human approval gate.

## Render alternative

If the owner later chooses Render, run the same API image and an appropriate worker service with privateRedis access and the sameSupabase/Snowflake contracts. Verify current service andworker plan limits before selection. Do not substitute a sleeping web-only process for durable jobs or assume analways-onworker is free. Update ADR002 andrerun hosted acceptance after changing hosting.

024 docs/ROLLBACK.md

# Rollback and recovery

Before each implementation prompt, commit a clean checkpoint and record the current schema and catalogue version. Revert only the intended commit after checking later dependencies. Never use a hard reset that discards unrelated work. Reverse applied migrations through tested forward compensating migrations; never reset a shared database.

For deployment, select the previous immutable API and worker image pair compatible with the current schema. Pause new jobs, allow or expire active leases, restart the old pair, and verify readiness before resuming. The web release must match the supported API contract. Rollback must preserve compatibility checks and human approval.

If catalogue activation has not committed, the old pointer remains active. A remote-only version can be reconciled by its hash and count. If an activated version must be reverted, validate the previous snapshot and stock freshness, then make a new audited activation. Historical approvals retain their original facts and evidence.

For reporting failures, retain pending PostgreSQL outbox events and retry with the same event IDs. For uncertain OpenAI completion, retain usage reservations until reconciliation. Redis loss does not remove durable jobs; rate-limited intake fails closed. To recover a lost host, restore the committed Compose configuration and secrets, then recover jobs through their leases. Rehearse restores in development before claiming backup recovery works.

025 docs/TEST_CHECKLIST.md

# Test strategy and acceptance gates

## Specification checks versus application tests

The kit validator checks references, schemas, prompt coverage and archive structure. It does not prove that the application works. The implementation agent must execute every named test as source is built. Never mark live Snowflake, OpenAI, RLS or hosted acceptance passed using mocks.

## Test layers

Unit tests cover Arabic normalization, serial boundaries, fitment filtering, supersession cycles, rank margins, allocation bounds, fact hashes, fixed transitions and redaction. Integration tests use real disposable PostgreSQL constraints, RLS, actor context reset, Storage policies, idempotency, approval races, job leases and catalogue activation. Contract tests compare the 77 REST operations, strict fields, Problem responses and frontend types.

Each of the 69 features has backend and frontend acceptance paths. Browser tests cover both languages, RTL, keyboard navigation, 360px layouts, themes, long content and four demos. Provider checks separately exercise Snowflake key-pair login, round-trip hashes and duplicate validation, plus OpenAI structured text/vision and allowance accounting. Hosted checks cover CORS, TLS, private ports, worker restart and observed latency.

## Required failure cases

| Failure | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Exact part number is incompatible | Exclude before ranking |
| Two candidates have close scores | Ask a question or require staff selection |
| OCR identifiers are unconfirmed | Do not resolve the machine |
| Quantity changes during processing | Discard old lease output |
| Two approvals race | Publish once for the current revision |
| Stock changes before approval | Return 409 and require replanning/review |
| Source version has duplicate keys | Do not activate |
| Remote upload succeeds but local commit fails | Keep old version active |
| Reporting acknowledgement is lost | Replay the same event ID without duplication |
| Redis is unavailable | Deny rate-limited intake; retain durable jobs |
| Provider completion is uncertain | Hold the usage reservation |
| Free allowance expires | Block live work; no paid fallback |
| Demo is reset during a job | Reject old-generation writes |
| Reviewer assignment changes | Remove previous reviewer access |
| Instructions are injected into text/photo | No privileged action occurs |

## Evidence and final gate

For every check, record command, environment, commit, time, expected result, actual result and sanitized logs. Accuracy requires a denominator; latency requires hardware and runtime context. A skip is not a pass. A resolver result is not a runtime build, and SQL parsing is not live policy validation. Do not remove required tests to obtain a green result.

During incremental development, CI validates completed prompt owners and requires that their named tests exist. The final release gate requires every feature, all 77 operations, and all mandatory tests. Live checks lacking account access remain visibly blocked; they cannot be replaced with fixture evidence.

026 docs/FIELD_GUIDE_MAP.md

# Collaboration practices

The original AI-Collaboration-Field-Guide.pdf remains in references for source review. The following practices apply its collaboration intent; these are not verbatim quotations from the source.

1. Explain product purpose in CONTEXT and PRD.
2. Establish architecture boundaries before feature edits.
3. Execute one sequenced prompt at a time.
4. Read existing legacy code before rewriting it.
5. Define typed contracts before UI assumptions.
6. Specify dependencies and exact installed versions.
7. Name source paths and creation ownership.
8. Make small independently reviewable commits.
9. Test behavior and negative boundaries.
10. Preserve actual failure evidence.
11. Maintain handover and session logs across sessions.
12. Keep security and cost constraints visible.
13. Separate model outputs from deterministic decisions.
14. Require human review before publication.
15. Verify artifacts and deployment rather than trusting generated claims.

ARCHITECTURE.md answers the eight architecture questions. Every implementation prompt includes context, contracts, logic, API flow, tests, commands, documentation, rollback and completion evidence.

030 docs/RECRUITER_GUIDE.md

# Recruiter project explanation

PartsIQ is a bilingual spare-parts enquiry platform. OpenAI extracts customer text and nameplate details. Python identifies equipment, filters compatible parts, plans warehouse quantities and validates the reply. Staff approve the final recommendation. Snowflake supplies versioned catalogue data and redacted reporting; Supabase provides transactional records, authentication and private files.

The engineering story is the boundary between probabilistic extraction and deterministic decisions. Demonstrate serial-range constraints, compatibility before ranking, revision-bound approval, job leases, idempotent REST writes and recoverable Snowflake synchronization. Explain why interactive requests use a validated relational cache and why Snowflake source constraints are validated explicitly.

Do not describe this as a multi-agent system or claim real distributor adoption without evidence. Add repository, deployed application, test receipts and recorded walkthrough links only when they exist. A fixture deployment demonstrates application behavior but must be labelled separately from live provider integration evidence.

031 docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md

# Recruiter walkthrough script

## Three minute version

First 30 seconds: explain the bilingual enquiry problem and human approval. Show the synthetic-data notice and single-backend architecture. Next 60 seconds: run the mixed-language photo scenario, confirm identifiers, and show compatibility evidence and the draft. Next 30 seconds: approve and display the published reply. Next 30 seconds: demonstrate a missing serial or incompatible part and show the system refusing to guess. Final 30 seconds: show the warehouse split, Snowflake source version and test/audit evidence. State which providers are live and which are fixtures.

## Eight minute version

Explain the problem and roles. Walk through chat, photo and confirmation. Show the fixed workflow and why agent routing is unnecessary. Demonstrate serial ambiguity and an incompatible exact part number. Compare candidate evidence and stock freshness. Edit an item and demonstrate approval invalidation. Approve and export the result. Show Snowflake source/reporting and the validated serving cache. Finish with measured tests, cost controls and single-host limitations.

## Recording checklist

Use synthetic data and clean browser profiles. Hide keys, JWTs, signed URLs and billing identifiers. Verify all four scenarios before recording. Include both languages and one failure path. Do not claim a video exists until recorded. Add captions and check published links. Accuracy claims require denominators; latency claims require actual hardware/runtime context.

033 brand/BRAND.md

# PartsIQ brand system

Use supplied falcon/gear/magnifier bilingual mark. Preserve aspect ratio; do not redraw the Arabic text. Primary navy#2B2D7F and gold#C59A45 are standardized tokens; the raster artwork also contains gradients and antialiasing. Gold is decorative/accent, not small text on white. Use navy for primary action, neutral surfaces and semantic state colours from tokens.json. Dark-mode muted/border overrides preserve readable contrast.

Typography: Noto Sans for English, Noto Sans Arabic for Arabic UI, Noto Naskh Arabic for Arabic PDF. Licensed font files and OFL notices are bundled. Use font-display: swap; self-host fonts; never depend on external PDF font fetch. Use bdi for part numbers and serials.

Use full lockup at minimum160CSSpx width in header/landing; icon-only at24/32px when space is constrained. Leave clear space equal to one-quarter icon width. Never stretch, crop critical mark elements, place on a busy photo or imply endorsement by a dealer. Small favicon uses supplied icon crop, not illegible full bilingual lockup.

Exports: favicon ICO16/32/48; PNG16/32/48/96; Apple180; PWA192/512; maskable192/512; social1200x630; profile1080; full logo320/640/1280. Existing supplied pack is preserved under assets. Asset manifest records actual dimensions and SHA256; use it rather than guessing file names. No authentic vector source was supplied, so no SVG is falsely presented as original artwork.

Prompt 18 copies every manifest-listed asset and fonts into apps/web/public/brand. PDF worker copies the same font bytes and logo into its image. Brand exports are already bundled; new raster editing is unnecessary.

035 docs/FLOW.md

# Fixed Python workflow

The controller is a deterministic transition table, not an LLM router. Persist state in workflow_runs and completed outputs in workflow_step_results. The unique key is enquiry_id plus revision. A job lease and a separate input hash fence every committed result.

| Current step | Condition | Next step | Function owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| intake | Text parsed and no image pending | identify or clarify | ai.extraction.extract_message |
| intake | Validated image requires reading | await_ocr | jobs.nameplate.read_nameplate |
| await_ocr | OCR result persisted | confirm | enquiries.extraction.confirm_nameplate |
| confirm | Customer confirms identifiers | identify | workflow.resolution.resolve_items |
| identify | Missing or conflicting machine details | clarify | enquiries.questions.clarification |
| identify | One configuration resolved for each item | search | search.service.SearchService |
| clarify | New answer accepted in new revision | intake or identify | enquiries.intake.append_message |
| search | No compatible result | needs_staff | workflow.resolution.resolve_items |
| search | Close candidates | choose | enquiries.questions.clarification |
| search | Unique sufficient match | plan | enquiries.fulfilment.plan_enquiry |
| choose | Current candidate chosen | plan | enquiries.revisions.choose_candidate |
| plan | Complete or explicitly short plan | draft | ai.reply.draft_slots |
| plan | Missing/stale inventory | needs_staff | enquiries.fulfilment.plan_enquiry |
| draft | Structured slots rendered | verify | enquiries.verification.verify_facts |
| verify | All checks pass | review | workflow.repository.commit_step |
| verify | Any rule fails | needs_staff | enquiries.verification.verify_facts |
| review | Current revision approved | complete | enquiries.approval.approve |
| review | Corrected/rejected | new revision or terminal rejection | enquiries.revisions or approval |

Each transition has a typed StepOutcome with reason_code and model-validated step data. The data envelope is not permission to store arbitrary provider output. Define a concrete payload model for each step using the provided IntakeResult, MachineView, CandidateList, PlanView, ReplySlots and VerificationResult contracts. Validate the matching payload before persistence.

## Persistence algorithm

Claim a due job with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a random lease token. Load enquiry/session and reject obsolete revision/generation. Under a short transaction, claim the matching workflow run. Release locks before calling OpenAI, Storage or Snowflake. Hash the exact step inputs and reuse only an identical completed result. Perform one bounded step. Reacquire row lock, recheck lease/revision/generation, write output and next state, append audit, then commit. Schedule the next step or park at a waiting state. Renew leases while healthy; never let an expired process finalize a result. Stop after20automatic transitions in one job.

No transaction remains open across a provider call. There is no promise of exactly-once external API execution; uncertain provider completions remain conservatively charged/reserved. Business publication is effectively once through idempotency and a unique recommendation-per-revision index.

## User changes

New facts or item choice invalidate derived data by creating a new revision. Preserve old outputs for audit but do not reuse them without matching input hash and source version. Assignment and notes need not change the extraction revision unless they alter facts. An assignment has its own audit event and immediate access effect. Reset increments demo generation and makes old jobs obsolete. User questions are code-owned bilingual templates and do not require staff approval because they make no final part recommendation.

## Cross-feature dependencies

Search and verification share one source of fitment truth. Draft rendering consumes VerifiedFacts only. Approval rechecks freshness and fact hash. PDF uses ApprovedSnapshot only. Analytics observes committed business events and cannot block approval. AI allowance remains local and authoritative even when traces or Snowflake reporting are unavailable.

036 docs/REQUIREMENTS.md

# Product requirements document

## Purpose and success criteria

PartsIQ helps customers describe equipment spare-part needs and helps staff prepare a defensible response. The system reduces manual interpretation and catalogue searching while keeping compatibility, quantity allocation and final approval under deterministic control. A successful recruiter demonstration shows the full enquiry journey, one ambiguity case, one incompatible request and one warehouse split, including visible provenance and human review.

Acceptance is behavioral rather than a claimed accuracy number: an incompatible exact-number match must never be recommended; unconfirmed photo identifiers must not drive matching; ambiguous candidates must not be silently selected; an unassigned reviewer must not see real enquiries; and a recommendation must not publish without a matching approved revision. Performance and extraction accuracy are measured later using the supplied evaluation plan.

## Actors and permissions

Public visitor reads the landing page and architecture. Anonymous demo customer owns an expiring demo session and can switch to reviewer presentation only for that session. Invited customer owns real enquiries when real onboarding is enabled. Reviewer sees assigned real enquiries and can correct, draft, approve or reject. Catalogue administrator stages, validates and publishes source versions. Administrator manages assignments, allowances, evaluation curation and aggregate reporting. Runtime worker identities are technical roles, not human roles.

## Main user journey

Customer creates an enquiry with destination warehouse and up to20 requested items. Optional images are privately uploaded, validated and read in the background. Structured extraction preserves the original message and source spans. The customer confirms photo identifiers and answers missing-information questions. Machine identification resolves one configuration. Search retrieves only explicitly compatible parts and supplies evidence. Close scores trigger a choice or review. Fulfilment combines repeated-part demand across items and reports availability, shortage and transfer estimates without reserving stock. A constrained draft is verified and presented to staff. Approval rechecks revision, catalogue and stock before atomically recording the decision and publishing the customer reply. Approved information can be exported as a bilingual enquiry PDF.

## Complete feature scope

Every feature below remains mandatory unless its behavior explicitly describes a capability flag, such as optional semantic ranking. Optional capability means implemented and testable with a transparent disabled mode, not silently omitted.

### F01 Branded landing

Explain the enquiry-to-approval journey; show synthetic-demo notice; expose Start demo and architecture links; display the supplied bilingual logo without stretching.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing repository link hides that action; logo has meaningful alternative text; no affiliation claim.

### F02 Demo scenarios and assets

Seed four deterministic scenarios: mixed-language photo, missing serial, incompatible part, local shortage; derive identifiers from seed 42; validate expected outcomes against generated records.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Reject a scenario whose expected part lacks compatibility; reject stock claims not supported by fixture quantities.

### F03 Demo role switching

Switch the presentation between customer and reviewer using the same anonymous identity and session; authorize review only for enquiries belonging to that active session.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Forged reviewer role never grants staff membership; another visitor's enquiry returns 404.

### F04 Demo isolation

Bind each session to verified anonymous Supabase identity; check generation and expiry on every read, write and worker completion; exclude demos from operational metrics by default.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Expired, reset and foreign sessions fail; missing identity context returns no rows.

### F05 Demo reset

Lock session; increment generation; cancel unfinished jobs from prior generation; enqueue Storage cleanup; keep minimal audit; create fresh scenario enquiries on explicit selection.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Late OCR from old generation cannot update current data; repeated reset idempotency key returns the same generation.

### F06 Responsive layouts

Support 360, 768, 1280 CSS-pixel widths; stack review panels; horizontally scroll comparison tables within their region; preserve sticky primary review actions without covering content.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No page-wide horizontal overflow; zoom 200 percent remains usable; mobile dialogs retain visible close action.

### F07 Arabic and English interface

Use a locale cookie and complete en/ar message catalogs; persist preference; set document lang and dir; isolate serials, numbers and part identifiers with bdi.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing translation fails tests; language switch preserves enquiry ID and unsent draft; mixed Arabic identifiers remain readable.

### F08 Light and dark themes

Use CSS semantic tokens; initialize from saved preference then system setting; expose accessible toggle; honor reduced motion and browser color-scheme.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No hydration mismatch; chart colors and focus rings meet contrast checks; storage-disabled browsers still work.

### F09 Bilingual chat

Accept Arabic, English and mixed text; preserve original message; detect preferred reply locale; render customer messages immediately after successful persistence.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Empty and oversized input returns validation error; HTML is escaped; retry does not duplicate a message.

### F10 Structured extraction

Extract item descriptions, quantities, urgency and machine hints with strict structured outputs; preserve source spans; missing quantity becomes a clarification rather than assumed order quantity.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown keys and invalid quantities reject the response; unsupported model output cannot progress to search.

### F11 Clarifying questions

Use workflow reason codes to choose code-owned bilingual questions; persist pending question; associate answer with item; rerun affected resolution only.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No final recommendation before approval; contradictory answer requires confirmation; repeat event creates one question.

### F12 Conversation memory

Persist all messages and typed current state; compact context using retained structured facts; resume by enquiry/revision; never mix customer sessions.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Restart retains unresolved questions; old revision events are ignored and audited; foreign thread ID denied.

### F13 Private uploads

Create pending attachment and unique object path; use signed upload; validate actual bytes and magic type after confirmation; strip EXIF and cap decoded pixels before OCR.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Wrong MIME, oversized content, image decompression bomb, duplicate confirmation and nonexistent object handled explicitly.

### F14 Nameplate OCR

Read validated nameplate via OpenAI vision; return model_text, serial_text, issues and source attachment; persist result only with current lease and revision.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unreadable fields remain null; vision instructions in photo are untrusted; timeout is bounded and creates recoverable status.

### F15 OCR confirmation

Show cropped or original nameplate beside extracted identifiers; require user confirm or correction; record actor and time; preserve leading zeros in serial text.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unconfirmed OCR never authorizes matching; blank corrected serial triggers missing-serial flow; stale confirmation returns 409.

### F16 Photo quality feedback

Check decodability, dimensions and blur heuristic before paid call; return actionable retake instructions; mark heuristic as advisory; allow a readable image despite noncritical blur warning.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unsupported format rejected; dark or low-resolution sample gets guidance; no fabricated OCR confidence percentage.

### F17 Multi-part enquiries

Track up to 20 items with independent quantity, machine, candidate selection and status; clarify individual items; verify aggregate allocation for repeated part requests.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: One unresolved item blocks final all-items approval; allocations across duplicate parts cannot double count available stock; zero quantity rejected.

### F18 Progress timeline

Show persisted stages, wait reason and last update; poll with bounded backoff; reconnect using server state; separate waiting for customer from waiting for staff.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No fake completed progress; failed poll retains last state and offers retry; hidden tabs reduce polling.

### F19 Enquiry history

Return cursor-paginated owned history with status and created time; filter active demo generation; link to full conversation; use stable created_at/id ordering.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Foreign owner ID ignored; invalid cursor returns 422; equal timestamps do not duplicate or skip records.

### F20 Machine identification

Preserve identify_machine logic for model, serial and rating; return resolved configuration or explicit missing/ambiguous status; normalize numeric serial only after preserving input.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Boundary serials match exactly one configuration; overlapping ranges fail Snowflake publication validation and PostgreSQL serving-cache insertion; conflicting hints never silently override.

### F21 Machine mismatch detection

Compare model and serial together; return mismatch reason with safe next question; prevent retrieval while identity unresolved.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Valid serial of a different model does not match requested model; nonnumeric serial handled without crashing.

### F22 Compatibility gate

Fetch authoritative fitment set first; rank only members; carry source_reference and catalogue version through every candidate.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: A perfect lexical match outside fitment is absent; empty fitment returns unavailable; blank provenance cannot be published.

### F23 Aliases and typo matching

Preserve Arabic normalization, part-number keys, phrase scoring and fuzzy token matching; remove machine terms using resolved model context.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Arabic part words are not removed as machine words; exact part number outranks unrelated fuzzy alias; normalization parity test matches SQL.

### F24 Semantic retrieval

Load one BGE-M3 encoder in the worker search module; use normalized 1024-d vectors; retain legacy weighted fusion; fall back to lexical on unavailable embedding path.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Wrong dimension rejected; no model loaded in API process; no semantic candidate outside compatible IDs.

### F25 Ranked candidates

Return top candidates with lexical/semantic evidence and deterministic tie order; compute runner-up margin before applying response limit.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Limit one still reports ambiguity; empty set returns no candidate; NaN scores rejected.

### F26 Ambiguity handling

Use tested score and margin thresholds in code; ask customer to distinguish fuel filter versus separator; allow staff to select only verified candidates.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: LLM cannot override low confidence; unavailable candidate choice returns 409; thresholds evaluated on labelled cases.

### F27 Match explanations

Show actual alias, machine configuration, supersession chain and fitment reference; derive explanations from search evidence rather than invented model prose.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Absent evidence shown as unavailable; user HTML is escaped; scores never labelled calibrated probability.

### F28 Compatibility references

Resolve source_reference to version-specific document and page; retain citation with every candidate and approval snapshot.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing source file blocks evidence viewer and flags review; mismatched version fails verification.

### F29 Evidence page viewer

Authorize assigned reviewer or own demo reviewer; request short-lived backend-signed PDF URL; open exact cited page; label synthetic document.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Customer receives reference only; arbitrary Storage key rejected; expired link can be renewed after authorization.

### F30 Old part numbers

Follow supersession chain with cycle protection; display old and current numbers; verify current successor has explicit fitment for resolved configuration.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Cycles rejected; inactive terminal part returns unavailable; inherited compatibility without source is rejected.

### F31 Candidate comparison

Compare two or three candidates from the same item/revision; show number, names, evidence and warehouse availability; selecting a candidate sends its ID, not browser-authored facts.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Foreign candidate or stale revision rejected; missing attribute shown as unavailable; keyboard navigation works.

### F32 Warehouse stock

Show available quantity as on_hand minus reserved; include timestamp and warehouse name; keep display and planner using same snapshot.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Negative stock blocked; stock unavailable never displayed as zero without explanation; unknown warehouse rejected.

### F33 Fulfilment planning

Allocate local stock first then reachable warehouses deterministically; compute shortage; use quantity units; do not reserve stock or create orders.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Total allocations never exceed request or stock; fractional quantities respect unit policy; unavailable transfer route cannot be invented.

### F34 Transfer estimates

Carry integer transfer_days from approved route; show estimate and source warehouse; local availability means zero transfer days.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No route gives unknown/unavailable plan rather than invented one-day promise; estimate labelled non-guaranteed.

### F35 Stock freshness

Compare stock timestamp with configurable freshness limit; mark stale data in review; re-read current stock during approval; invalidate plan when allocation no longer possible.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Future timestamp flagged; changed stock returns 409 and reruns planning; stale stock never becomes a delivery guarantee.

### F36 Staff inbox

List assigned operational enquiries and own active demo enquiries; filter status, priority, overdue and text; paginate stably; show counts in same access scope.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unassigned real enquiries hidden from reviewer; admin can see all; filters do not leak global counts.

### F37 Review workspace

Assemble current extraction, items, candidates, evidence, stock, draft and timeline; show verification failures; separate staff-only notes from customer messages.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Missing panels show explicit empty states; stale revision disables approval; unassigned reviewer receives 404.

### F38 Correct extracted details

Lock enquiry; compare expected revision; apply typed allowed corrections; increment revision; invalidate derived selections/draft/approval; enqueue recomputation; record before and after.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown field rejected; old revision returns 409; correction cannot directly set approved status or invent candidate facts.

### F39 Review actions

Approve only verified current draft; edit prose through controlled schema then reverify; reject with reason; record actor and idempotency key.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Double-click publishes once; concurrent edit defeats stale approval; failed verification blocks publication.

### F40 Approval invalidation

Bind approval to revision and verified fact hash; any identity, quantity, selection or catalogue-sensitive change requires new draft and approval.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Old approval cannot authorize new revision; late workflow update cannot overwrite approved current state.

### F41 Internal notes

Append reviewer notes with author and timestamp; show only in staff workspace; prohibit customer/PDF exposure; escape rendered content.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Empty or over-4000-character note rejected; customer route never includes note text; unassigned staff denied.

### F42 Assignments

Admin assigns active reviewer or unassigns; persist assignment history atomically; access changes immediately; demo reviewer access remains session-scoped.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Non-admin assignment denied; disabled/nonreviewer assignee rejected; previous reviewer loses access on next request.

### F43 Overdue indicators

Set due_at using configurable urgent/normal thresholds; display overdue only for unresolved states; sort overdue first when requested; store all times UTC.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Approved/rejected items never overdue; daylight-saving display does not change deadline; thresholds not described as contractual SLA.

### F44 Conversation summary

Produce staff-only concise summary from authorized messages and confirmed fields; store message IDs and revision; use shared budget wrapper; regenerate on relevant change.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Outdated summary labelled stale; instructions inside messages ignored; exhausted budget leaves full conversation available.

### F45 Reply drafting

Generate greeting, explanation and closing as structured slots; code inserts all numbers and allocations; choose Arabic or English from confirmed preference.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unapproved critical facts never rendered; unsupported slots rejected; provider failure permits staff-authored controlled draft.

### F46 Verification gate

Check item/configuration/candidate membership, provenance, catalogue version, selected quantities and allocation bounds; compute canonical fact hash; store named rule results.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown part, incompatible part, stale catalogue, oversold plan and hidden extra item each fail a specific rule.

### F47 Human publication gate

Only approval service inserts recommendation messages; lock enquiry and recheck role, revision and verification; unique publication index prevents duplicates.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No background job write tool can publish; database rejects recommendation lacking matching approved decision.

### F48 Input isolation

Treat customer text, OCR and imported evidence as data; separate trusted instructions; bound inputs, transitions, steps and output size; never execute model-produced templates.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Prompt injection cannot call privileged functions, change roles or reveal secrets; model result with rogue instructions remains inert.

### F49 Audit trail

Append actor, request, entity, revision and minimal before/after metadata for AI suggestions and human changes; redact secrets and full sensitive payloads.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Application UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE fail; audit write failure rolls back approval; database-owner powers documented honestly.

### F50 Durable workflows

Persist workflow_runs and workflow_step_results in PostgreSQL; run a fixed Python transition table with durable jobs; serialize each enquiry and fence completion by revision and lease token; recover after restart without LangGraph.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Duplicate jobs cannot repeat publication; stale revisions are discarded; interrupted steps resume from committed results; no LLM chooses the next step.

### F51 Background jobs

Persist job before Redis dispatch; dispatcher claims by ID; sweeper redispatches pending/expired jobs; worker handles OCR, PDF, imports and cleanup.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Redis loss does not lose DB job; unavailable Redis rate limiter fails closed; heavy work never blocks HTTP intake.

### F52 Retry and deduplication

Claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; assign lease token; heartbeat; retry transient errors with backoff up to max attempts; fence final writes by lease token.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Expired worker cannot commit; permanent validation failure not retried; provider timeout marked uncertain and budget held conservatively.

### F53 Graceful failures

Map stable error codes to bilingual recovery guidance; distinguish validation, quota, service outage and staff-required states; preserve user input.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No raw stack traces or keys; retry only safe idempotent action; search lexical fallback clearly reported.

### F54 Access and permissions

Verify Supabase issuer, audience, signature, expiry; derive identity server-side; enforce assigned-only review; keep credentials server-side; disable public real-client signup.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Forged role claim ignored; missing context denies rows; preview cannot reach prod database; demo cannot publish shared catalogue.

### F55 Saved machines

Save confirmed model and serial with user label; list own active entries; archive entry; prefill a new enquiry but re-identify against current catalogue.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Duplicate label permitted with distinct ID; foreign ID denied; stale configuration never reused as authoritative.

### F56 Repeat enquiry

Copy customer request and confirmed hints into a new enquiry; issue new ID/revision; link origin in audit; run matching, stock and review again.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Never copy approval, allocation, draft or signed file URL; source ownership required; repeated submission deduplicated.

### F57 Catalogue browser

Read published catalogue with model/category/text filters; page results; show part detail and supersession; staff can inspect fitment and sources.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No unpublished import rows exposed; missing number returns 404; literal query cannot become SQL.

### F58 Catalogue imports

Read CSV UTF-8 or XLSX without evaluating formulas; validate row schema, references, serial overlap, supersession cycles and source evidence; show dry-run report; explicit admin publish. Stage a version in Snowflake, validate all relationships explicitly and only then activate a validated PostgreSQL serving snapshot.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Invalid batch changes no published data; file with macros/formulas rejected; 50000-row and 10MiB limits enforced; public demo cannot publish.

### F59 Catalogue versioning

Store immutable versioned catalogue records in Snowflake; verify record counts and canonical SHA256; stage the PostgreSQL serving snapshot; atomically switch the active version in a PostgreSQL transaction; retain published historical records; reconcile partial remote writes.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Two publishers cannot leave two active versions; failed publish rolls back; old approval retains immutable evidence snapshot.

### F60 Missing-parts queue

Record unresolved item once; allow assigned staff to mark investigating, resolved or unavailable with note; link back to enquiry; no automatic catalogue creation.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Resolved status requires staff explanation; foreign item denied; empty search result is not fabricated stock.

### F61 Enquiry PDF

Export approved revision only; render logo, bilingual customer text, verified selections, estimates and references; embed Arabic fonts; store private object and signed download.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Exclude notes and secrets; stale or unapproved revision rejected; long Arabic names wrap without clipping; no prices or quotation title.

### F62 Labelled evaluations

Include four demos plus Arabic, typo, serial-boundary, ambiguity, stock and injection cases; record expected compatible set and clarification outcome; run deterministic suite without API calls.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No self-reported model confidence as accuracy; evaluation fixture disjoint from examples used in prompts; failures keep actual output.

### F63 Metrics dashboard

Show volume, status, review time, clarification and labelled accuracy with denominators; separate demo traffic; filter time window; scope reviewer data to assignments. Export redacted aggregate events to Snowflake through an outbox and show reporting freshness separately from live operational counts.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Zero denominator displays unavailable; no fabricated percentage; demo traffic never silently improves operational metrics.

### F64 Latency and AI cost

Measure stages with monotonic clock; log model/token usage and estimated cost; reserve confirmed free credit before each attempt; expose consumed/reserved allowance.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Unknown price or expired credit blocks calls; concurrent reservations cannot exceed cap; API key validity never implies free credit.

### F65 Correction feedback

List authorized before/after corrections; let admin curate anonymized labelled eval cases; record reviewer and source revision; never auto-train on unreviewed edits.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Private text excluded from exported fixtures; duplicate case source detected; unreviewed correction cannot become ground truth.

### F66 Tests and CI

Run service-isolated Python tests, frontend checks, RLS integration and deterministic evals; build images; require explicit environment approval for deployment; pin action SHAs.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No prod DB in tests; no secret available to untrusted fork jobs; failed gate blocks deployment.

### F67 Traces

Propagate request/enquiry/job IDs; capture stage timing and safe status; export optional Langfuse traces with payload redaction; operate normally when tracing unavailable.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No raw key or full photo logged; exporter outage never breaks approval; budget accounting remains local and authoritative.

### F68 Recruiter documentation

Write concise overview, real architecture, quick start, demo paths, tests, trade-offs and limitations; link measured evidence; explain deterministic decisions and ordinary Python functions.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: No invented accuracy, uptime, client relationship or production adoption; distinguish implementation status from specification.

### F69 Demo walkthrough

Create 3-minute and 8-minute scripts covering happy path, missing serial, incompatibility, stock split and human review; include recording checklist and captions.

Acceptance and failure boundaries: Do not claim video exists until recorded; use synthetic data; show failure handling and reset; verify links before sending recruiters.

## Nonfunctional requirements

Security: server-verified identity, scope checks, RLS, private files, least-privilege data roles, redacted logging and no model-authorized writes. Durability: database-backed jobs, leases, fencing, idempotent API writes and recoverable partial Snowflake synchronization. Language: Arabic/English UI and replies, mixed-script identifiers, bidi isolation and bundled Arabic PDF fonts. Accessibility: keyboard operation, visible focus, reduced motion, 200 percent zoom and360px minimum layout. Maintainability: typed models, one domain implementation per rule, versioned migrations and explicit test evidence.

Provisional performance goals are local acceptance budgets, not measured claims: API writes should acknowledge without waiting for AI or warehouse work; provider operations have bounded timeouts; polling uses backoff; optional embeddings cannot prevent lexical readiness. Benchmark the actual host before setting public latency claims. The paid budget is zero; the system requires confirmed free allowance before live provider calls. Real-client retention is an onboarding decision; until it is recorded, real onboarding stays disabled. Demo access expires after24hours and background cleanup follows the documented policy.

## Exclusions

No voice input, quotation builder, prices, payments, orders, stock reservations, automatic WhatsApp/email sending, multi-agent routing, autonomous SQL generation or automatic training on staff corrections. No claim of perpetual free cloud hosting. No invented partnership with equipment distributors.

# 00 Repository bootstrap and legacy characterization

## GOAL
Unpack references/legacy-backend.zip in a temporary directory and calculate SHA256 for every original file.

## CONTEXT AND PREREQUISITES
The product is a bilingual spare-parts enquiry and human-review application. Snowflake stores versioned source catalogue data and redacted reporting events; Supabase supplies authentication, private files and PostgreSQL operational records. A validated PostgreSQL catalogue mirror supports compatibility checks and fast interactive reads. One FastAPI package and one background worker run the application. OpenAI extracts text/photos and writes constrained prose; ordinary Python controls all decisions. No multi-agent framework is part of this build.

Read AGENTS.md, docs/PRD.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/CONSTRAINTS.md, docs/TECH_SPEC.md, docs/REST_API.md and docs/WORKFLOW.md. Foundation 18 copies the supplied web manifest and lock before `corepack pnpm --dir apps/web install --frozen-lockfile`. Do not install LangGraph, LangChain, CrewAI or an agent SDK. Snowflake uses snowflake-connector-python==4.8.0 with fixed SQL and bound parameters. OpenAI uses openai==3.19.2; FastAPI==0.135.1, Pydantic==2.12.5, asyncpg==0.31.0 and httpx==0.28.1 supply the application boundaries. ## TYPED CONTRACTS
```python
def inspect_legacy(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]
def run_checks(prompt_id: str) -> int
```

Contract models are defined in spec/contracts.py and spec/api_models.py. Legacy IdentifyRequest, IdentifyResponse, PartSearchRequest and PartSearchResponse remain in partsiq.search.schemas from the characterized legacy code. Path IDs are UUID except numeric catalogue IDs. Monetary usage and quantities use Decimal; timestamps are timezone-aware UTC. Settings is a pydantic-settings BaseSettings class generated from spec/environment.json. Return domain results; convert them to HTTP only in a route adapter. No domain function accepts an unverified actor supplied in a request body.

## IMPLEMENTATION STEPS
1. Unpack references/legacy-backend.zip in a temporary directory and calculate SHA256 for every original file.
2. Read its AGENTS.md before moving code.
3. Keep that archive unchanged.
4. Map identification.py, lexical.py, fulfilment.py, repository.py, service.py and schemas.py into apps/api/partsiq/search; adapt absolute app imports to partsiq.search.
5. Preserve the original function arguments and return semantics behind explicit adapters.
6. Run the legacy tests before changing behavior and record actual failures.
7. Create one Python package named partsiq; API and worker import it.
8. Create test fixtures and a prompt-aware runner that reads spec/build-order.json, finds the exact named tests and fails if a named test file is absent or every case is skipped.
9. Do not create separate gateway/search/orchestrator servers.
10. Configure Python 3.12 and Node 22.22.0.
11. Keep all implementation docs under docs and all generated application files in the ownership manifest.

Inject provider and database adapters so unit tests use deterministic fakes and integration tests use disposable services. Do not make network calls while holding an enquiry row lock. Separate external work from final fenced persistence. Every irreversible business mutation needs an audit record in the same transaction. Search/read operations must use the validated active catalogue version, never an arbitrary latest Snowflake row. Add explicit bounded timeouts for every dependency and map known failures to stable error codes.

## REST API AND DATA FLOW
The only public API is FastAPI under `/v1`. `apps/api/partsiq/api/router.py` includes feature routers created later. This foundation supplies domain functions; it must not invent additional competing endpoints. Read spec/endpoints.json for exact methods, resource paths, models and owners. Browser → verified route dependency → feature application function → this domain module → repository. Slow work is represented by a committed jobs row and a202 response. Worker → fixed transition table → domain function → lease-fenced PostgreSQL update. Snowflake synchronization is a separate job; no distributed transaction spans Snowflake and Supabase.

## VALIDATION AND FAILURES
Never remove compatible-set filtering, provenance, revision checks, assigned-only real review or own-session demo isolation. Never make an LLM choose a machine, authorize a part, approve, publish, execute SQL or invoke a write tool. Do not add voice, quotation builder, order creation, inventory reservation or external-message sending. A known part number is not sufficient evidence of fitment. Free keys are not proof of available credit. No paid fallback or account upgrade is authorized. Keep live providers disabled until their dedicated allowance and expiry have been confirmed.

Missing auth is401; insufficient role is403; a foreign scoped resource is404; stale revision, changed idempotency payload or stale catalogue is409; invalid typed input is422; request quota is429; a required unavailable dependency is503. Use Problem.code for machine-readable behavior and request_id for diagnosis. Do not expose database errors, secrets, private object paths or provider responses. A failed dependency must not be reported as an empty successful result.

## TESTS
Create `tests/foundations/test_00.py` with fixtures for the exact contracts above. Test the normal algorithm described in IMPLEMENTATION STEPS, each rejected boundary described there, and dependency failure without partial business writes. For data mutations use a rollback assertion and verify the audit event. For async work simulate an expired lease and a new revision before completion. For schema/infrastructure steps assert the actual SQL, configuration and installed versions rather than mocking the check itself. Keep network tests explicitly marked and never run them against production. Record separate unit, integration and hosted outcomes; no skipped required case may be called passed.

## COMMANDS AND EXPECTED RESULTS
Run `python tools/run_checks.py --prompt 00`. Expected: all named files exist, the selected tests execute, and exit status0 follows only when every required assertion passes. Run `uv run ruff check apps/api tests` and `uv run mypy apps/api/partsiq` when the package exists; fix new errors before continuing. For frontend changes run `corepack pnpm --dir apps/web test --run` and `corepack pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`. Do not assert a fixed passing test count before executing tests. Save stdout/stderr with credentials redacted in `evidence/00/`.

## MANUAL CHECK
Exercise this module through the nearest available caller using the synthetic fixture. Inspect the input, typed output, persisted revision, source version and request ID. Repeat with one invalid input and one unavailable dependency. If this is an infrastructure prompt, verify the real account/host receipt; lack of account access is blocked, not passed. UI checks include English, Arabic, 360px width, keyboard navigation and200 percent zoom. Do not display test-only data as real client inventory.

## DOCUMENTATION UPDATES
Update docs/HANDOVER.md with step00, actual changed paths, commands, results and the next build-order ID. Append docs/SESSION_LOG.md rather than replacing previous failures. Record source/schema changes in docs/TECH_SPEC.md and the relevant ADR. Update corresponding feature traces only after their acceptance tests pass. Add runtime API changes to the canonical specification and prove contract parity. Keep all claims about accuracy, cost and latency tied to measured evidence.

## ROLLBACK AND COMMIT
Create a clean checkpoint commit before this step. Commit only this prompt as `feat(bootstrap): implement foundation 00 repository bootstrap and legacy characterization`. Revert that exact commit after checking for dependent later changes. Applied database schema changes require a forward compensating migration; never reset shared Supabase or delete audit/history. Restore the previous active catalogue pointer only after validating its snapshot and stock freshness. Remote orphaned Snowflake versions stay unactivated for reconciliation. Rollback provider configuration without enabling a paid fallback.

## COMPLETION EVIDENCE
Report implemented signatures, caller/callee wiring, test commands, actual pass/fail output, manual observations, commit SHA and unresolved blockers. The coding agent must inspect its own diff and confirm no scope was silently removed. No runtime behavior is complete merely because this specification exists. Continue only when its dependencies are usable or clearly report the narrow blocker.

## IMPLEMENTATION STEPS

2. Copy each SQL file into supabase/migrations preserving exact ordering; do not apply removed checkpoint migrations.
3. Preserve legacy PostgreSQL overlap, cycle, unique, foreign-key and append-only controls.
4. Snowflake versions are remote immutable source records; PostgreSQL owns the single active serving pointer.
5. Read and validate a complete remote version outside a database lock, then acquire the catalogue advisory transaction lock, compare expected_active, upsert stable numeric IDs and reconcile rows in dependency order.
6. Never delete a referenced historical part or configuration.
7. Mark removed records inactive and keep immutable catalogue_records for old decisions.
8. All search reads must filter the active catalogue_records keyset, because historical rows remain in legacy tables.
9. Materialize the relational cache and switch catalogue_versions in one transaction.
10. A remote successful upload followed by local failure remains unactivated and is safe to reconcile.
11. Capture migration checksums and actual constraints; never claim a Snowflake PK protects integrity.
12. Runtime role groups separate API, workflow, worker, search and publisher permissions without requiring different services.

```python
class SearchService: async def identify(self, request: IdentifyRequest) -> IdentifyResponse
```

## IMPLEMENTATION STEPS
1. Port characterized legacy pure functions without changing scores accidentally.
2. Every query pins a catalogue version and uses its validated serving keyset.
3. Identify a single configuration before loading fitment; ambiguous identity yields needs_information.
4. Compute compatible IDs first and filter before lexical or semantic ranking.
5. Normalize Arabic variants, diacritics and tatweel with reviewed mappings; preserve part-number strings.
6. Keep machine words separate from part words.
7. Use existing phrase and typo scoring and explain contributing aliases.
8. BGE-M3 runs only within the worker search module, one CPU encoder per process; API handlers never load it.
9. Normalize1024-dimensional vectors, validate dimension and finite values, and calculate similarity only for compatible parts.
10. Optional embedding unavailability gives a labelled lexical fallback.
11. Compute runner-up margin before top-k truncation.
12. Follow old-number chains with a visited set and require explicit fitment on the final active part.
13. Allocate repeated requested parts together across items so stock cannot be counted twice.

3. Compute canonical input SHA256.
4. Reuse a completed step only when its input hash and revision match.
5. Call the appropriate domain function directly.
6. Reacquire lock and commit output only if the lease token, revision and session generation still match; stale output is discarded and audited.
7. Persist workflow_step_results and next step atomically.
8. A process crash after an external call but before commit may require another attempt; preserve uncertain AI usage reservations rather than claiming exactly-once provider invocation.
9. Missing facts pause in clarify; unreadable photo pauses in confirm; ambiguous ranking pauses in choose; verified draft pauses in review.
10. Only approval publishes.
11. Limit automatic transitions to20 per job and send unexpected loops to needs_staff.
12. Resume requires a new message, confirmation, choice or authorized retry event.

9. Retry only transient timeout/429/5xx with jittered backoff and honor Retry-After.
10. Invalid input and authorization failures are terminal.
11. Never put complete photos, credentials or raw prompts in Redis messages.

## TYPED CONTRACTS
```python
async def read_nameplate(lease: JobLease, image: ImageInfo) -> NameplateResult
async def confirm_nameplate(actor: ActorContext, enquiry_id: UUID, command: ConfirmExtraction) -> EnquiryView
```

Contract models are defined in spec/contracts.py and spec/api_models.py. Legacy IdentifyRequest, IdentifyResponse, PartSearchRequest and PartSearchResponse remain in partsiq.search.schemas from the characterized legacy code. Path IDs are UUID except numeric catalogue IDs. Monetary usage and quantities use Decimal; timestamps are timezone-aware UTC. Settings is a pydantic-settings BaseSettings class generated from spec/environment.json. Return domain results; convert them to HTTP only in a route adapter. No domain function accepts an unverified actor supplied in a request body.

## IMPLEMENTATION STEPS
1. Read only the sanitized private image produced by storage validation.
2. Send it to the approved OpenAI vision model through the shared budget wrapper and Responses API input_image.
3. Limit image bytes, pixels and output fields.
4. Text printed on the image is data, including any attempted instructions.
5. Parse model_text, serial_text and explicit issues; preserve leading zeros and do not fabricate a confidence percentage.
6. Keep the attachment ID code-owned.
7. Store OCR output only with current lease and revision, then pause for user confirmation.
8. Confirmation may correct either identifier and records the actor, time and source attachment.
9. If serial is not visible, allow a missing serial value and ask the normal identification clarification rather than blocking confirmation forever.
10. Reject contradictory or stale confirmation with 409.
11. Never match an unconfirmed machine from the photo.

Inject provider and database adapters so unit tests use deterministic fakes and integration tests use disposable services. Do not make network calls while holding an enquiry row lock. Separate external work from final fenced persistence. Every irreversible business mutation needs an audit record in the same transaction. Search/read operations must use the validated active catalogue version, never an arbitrary latest Snowflake row. Add explicit bounded timeouts for every dependency and map known failures to stable error codes.

## REST API AND DATA FLOW
The only public API is FastAPI under `/v1`. `apps/api/partsiq/api/router.py` includes feature routers created later. This foundation supplies domain functions; it must not invent additional competing endpoints. Read spec/endpoints.json for exact methods, resource paths, models and owners. Browser → verified route dependency → feature application function → this domain module → repository. Slow work is represented by a committed jobs row and a202 response. Worker → fixed transition table → domain function → lease-fenced PostgreSQL update. Snowflake synchronization is a separate job; no distributed transaction spans Snowflake and Supabase.

## VALIDATION AND FAILURES
Never remove compatible-set filtering, provenance, revision checks, assigned-only real review or own-session demo isolation. Never make an LLM choose a machine, authorize a part, approve, publish, execute SQL or invoke a write tool. Do not add voice, quotation builder, order creation, inventory reservation or external-message sending. A known part number is not sufficient evidence of fitment. Free keys are not proof of available credit. No paid fallback or account upgrade is authorized. Keep live providers disabled until their dedicated allowance and expiry have been confirmed.

Missing auth is401; insufficient role is403; a foreign scoped resource is404; stale revision, changed idempotency payload or stale catalogue is409; invalid typed input is422; request quota is429; a required unavailable dependency is503. Use Problem.code for machine-readable behavior and request_id for diagnosis. Do not expose database errors, secrets, private object paths or provider responses. A failed dependency must not be reported as an empty successful result.

## TESTS
Create `tests/foundations/test_16.py` with fixtures for the exact contracts above. Test the normal algorithm described in IMPLEMENTATION STEPS, each rejected boundary described there, and dependency failure without partial business writes. For data mutations use a rollback assertion and verify the audit event. For async work simulate an expired lease and a new revision before completion. For schema/infrastructure steps assert the actual SQL, configuration and installed versions rather than mocking the check itself. Keep network tests explicitly marked and never run them against production. Record separate unit, integration and hosted outcomes; no skipped required case may be called passed.

Run `uv run ruff check apps/api tests` and `uv run mypy apps/api/partsiq` when the package exists; fix new errors before continuing. For frontend changes run `corepack pnpm --dir apps/web test --run` and `corepack pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`. Do not assert a fixed passing test count before executing tests. Repeat with one invalid input and one unavailable dependency. If this is an infrastructure prompt, verify the real account/host receipt; lack of account access is blocked, not passed. Record source/schema changes in docs/TECH_SPEC.md and the relevant ADR. Update corresponding feature traces only after their acceptance tests pass. Add runtime API changes to the canonical specification and prove contract parity. Keep all claims about accuracy, cost and latency tied to measured evidence.

## ROLLBACK AND COMMIT
Create a clean checkpoint commit before this step. Commit only this prompt as `feat(vision): implement foundation 16 nameplate reading and human confirmation`. Revert that exact commit after checking for dependent later changes. Applied database schema changes require a forward compensating migration; never reset shared Supabase or delete audit/history. # F04 Demo isolation

## GOAL
Implement the complete demo isolation behavior in the single-workflow Snowflake edition. Bind each session to verified anonymous Supabase identity; check generation and expiry on every read, write and worker completion; exclude demos from operational metrics by default.

## CONTEXT AND PREREQUISITES
The product is a bilingual spare-parts enquiry and human-review application. Snowflake stores versioned source catalogue data and redacted reporting events; Supabase supplies authentication, private files and PostgreSQL operational records. A validated PostgreSQL catalogue mirror supports compatibility checks and fast interactive reads. One FastAPI package and one background worker run the application. OpenAI extracts text/photos and writes constrained prose; ordinary Python controls all decisions. No multi-agent framework is part of this build.

This feature extends foundations00–20 and follows F03. Read docs/PRD.md for the user outcome, docs/REST_API.md for transport rules, docs/DATA_OWNERSHIP.md for persistence, docs/WORKFLOW.md for state changes, and docs/SECURITY.md for access. This feature belongs to `api` at product level but runs inside the common application; ownership does not imply a separate service or agent. Preserve the behavior of all previously completed features.

Reuse foundation-installed packages; this feature introduces no floating dependency. Backend: FastAPI==0.135.1 with APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException and response_model; Pydantic==2.12.5 with Field and model_validate_json; asyncpg==0.31.0 with parameterized queries and explicit transactions; httpx==0.28.1 for bounded dependency calls. Tests: pytest==9.0.2 and pytest-asyncio==1.3.0. Frontend: the exact Next.js, React, Zod, next-intl, Vitest and Testing Library versions in spec/web-package.json. Run `uv pip sync spec/python-requirements.lock` and `corepack pnpm --dir apps/web install --frozen-lockfile` only if dependencies are not already synchronized. Snowflake access belongs to the catalogue/reporting adapter, not this browser feature. No extra agent library is allowed.

## FILES AND OWNERSHIP
- `apps/api/partsiq/features/f04_demo_isolation.py`: application facade connecting this feature to foundation domain functions.
- `apps/web/src/features/f04_demo_isolation/Panel.tsx`: accessible bilingual feature panel and its loading/error/empty states.
- `tests/features/test_f04.py`: feature acceptance tests; exercise the real public entry point with isolated fixtures.
- `apps/web/tests/features/f04.test.tsx`: feature acceptance tests; exercise the real public entry point with isolated fixtures.
- `apps/api/partsiq/api/f04_demo_isolation.py`: FastAPI route adapter with declared authorization and response model.

Register its router in `apps/api/partsiq/api/router.py` after the new module exists. Mount the panel in CustomerShell, StaffShell or the catalogue/admin page according to the access level. Extend existing en/ar dictionaries with namespaced keys `f04`; do not duplicate whole dictionaries. Record modifications to shared files in the handover. Add no second implementation of compatibility, approval, budget accounting or Snowflake access.

## TYPED CONTRACTS
```python
async def f04_require_demo_session(actor: ActorContext, session_id: UUID) -> DemoSession
async def f04_create_session(actor: ActorContext, idempotency_key: UUID) -> DemoSession
```

```python
class DemoSession(Contract):
    id: UUID
    generation: int = Field(ge=1)
    expires_at: datetime
```

Shared nested models are fully defined in spec/contracts.py and spec/api_models.py; copy their types rather than weakening them to unvalidated dictionaries. For a UI panel define `export function Panel(props: {enquiryId?: string; locale: 'en' | 'ar'; readOnly: boolean}): React.JSX.Element`. For a pure internal feature use `FeatureContext` with request_id, actor, enquiry_id, revision and `FeatureOutcome` with passed, code, details, as defined in spec/api_models.py. ReadOnly is a UI affordance; backend authorization remains mandatory. All serials and part numbers remain strings. Serialize Decimal as strings and UUID/datetime through the shared models.

## IMPLEMENTATION STEPS
1. Read the existing domain implementation and its tests. Write down the current caller and the expected persisted outcome for F04; use the canonical endpoint owner rather than adding another path.
2. Implement the facade signature above. Derive actor identity from the verified dependency, load the scoped enquiry/item when relevant, and reject a path/body ID mismatch before querying private data. A route must never accept an arbitrary actor, role, table name or Storage path from JSON.
3. Bind each session to verified anonymous Supabase identity.
4. Check generation and expiry on every read, write and worker completion.
5. Exclude demos from operational metrics by default.
6. Build the response from persisted current-revision records. Avoid returning internal notes, raw provider payloads, keys or object credentials. Use response_model filtering as an additional check, not as the only authorization boundary.
7. Wire the frontend through apiFetch and the exact response schema. Implement loading, empty, success, validation error, stale revision, forbidden and dependency-unavailable states where they apply. Disable duplicate submit while pending and keep a stable idempotency key for an explicit retry of the same operation.
8. Re-fetch the authoritative resource after a successful mutation. Do not optimistically display approval, stock availability or completed OCR before the server confirms it. On409 preserve the user input, show that data changed, and require a fresh intentional action using the new revision.
9. Attach request ID to logs and append an audit event for business changes inside the transaction. Measurements use monotonic durations and UTC event timestamps. Any reporting export is redacted and goes through analytics_outbox rather than a second uncoordinated remote write.

- `GET /v1/demo/sessions/{session_id}` → `f04_require_demo_session`; request `None` (no body); response `DemoSession`, HTTP 200; access `demo`.
- `POST /v1/demo/sessions` → `f04_create_session`; request `None` (no body); response `DemoSession`, HTTP 201; access `demo`.

# F09 Bilingual chat

## GOAL
Implement the complete bilingual chat behavior in the single-workflow Snowflake edition. Accept Arabic, English and mixed text; preserve original message; detect preferred reply locale; render customer messages immediately after successful persistence.

## CONTEXT AND PREREQUISITES
The product is a bilingual spare-parts enquiry and human-review application. Snowflake stores versioned source catalogue data and redacted reporting events; Supabase supplies authentication, private files and PostgreSQL operational records. A validated PostgreSQL catalogue mirror supports compatibility checks and fast interactive reads. One FastAPI package and one background worker run the application. OpenAI extracts text/photos and writes constrained prose; ordinary Python controls all decisions. No multi-agent framework is part of this build.

Snowflake access belongs to the catalogue/reporting adapter, not this browser feature. No extra agent library is allowed.

Register its router in `apps/api/partsiq/api/router.py` after the new module exists. Mount the panel in CustomerShell, StaffShell or the catalogue/admin page according to the access level. ## TYPED CONTRACTS
```python
async def f09_create_enquiry(actor: ActorContext, command: EnquiryCreate, idempotency_key: UUID) -> EnquiryView
async def f09_get_enquiry(actor: ActorContext, enquiry_id: UUID) -> EnquiryView
```

```python
class EnquiryCreate(Contract):
    text: str = Field(min_length=1,max_length=12000)
    locale: Locale
    destination_warehouse_id: int = Field(gt=0)
    session_id: UUID | None = None

class EnquiryView(Contract):
    id: UUID
    revision: int
    status: Literal['received','processing','needs_information','awaiting_review','approved','rejected','failed']
    messages: list[MessageView]
    item_ids: list[UUID]
    catalogue_version_id: UUID | None
    updated_at: datetime
```

Shared nested models are fully defined in spec/contracts.py and spec/api_models.py; copy their types rather than weakening them to unvalidated dictionaries. For a UI panel define `export function Panel(props: {enquiryId?: string; locale: 'en' | 'ar'; readOnly: boolean}): React.JSX.Element`. For a pure internal feature use `FeatureContext` with request_id, actor, enquiry_id, revision and `FeatureOutcome` with passed, code, details, as defined in spec/api_models.py. ReadOnly is a UI affordance; backend authorization remains mandatory. All serials and part numbers remain strings. Serialize Decimal as strings and UUID/datetime through the shared models.

## IMPLEMENTATION STEPS
1. Read the existing domain implementation and its tests. Write down the current caller and the expected persisted outcome for F09; use the canonical endpoint owner rather than adding another path.
